items.action: State that the minimum age to register is 16 in England and Northern Ireland and 14 in Scotland and Wales, and limit the age-18 rule to elections such as general elections.
items.reason: Young people in Scotland and Wales would be wrongly told they are too young to register, and 16 and 17-year-olds there would be wrongly told they can't vote in most elections.

problems.claim: Must be 16 or over to register (18 to vote in most elections).
problems.note: The minimum age of 16 applies only in England and Northern Ireland (it is 14 in Scotland and Wales), and the text gives 18 only for particular elections, such as general elections, not as a rule for most elections.

items.name: Electoral roll update
items.text: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).
items.action: Say Commonwealth citizens need permission to enter or stay, and that in England and Northern Ireland only certain EU citizens can vote in local elections.
items.reason: Some EU citizens in England and Northern Ireland would be wrongly told they can vote in local elections, and Commonwealth citizens without permission to stay could wrongly think they qualify.

problems.claim: British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen (EU citizens can vote in local elections).
problems.note: The text supports British, Irish and Commonwealth citizens (Commonwealth only with permission to enter or stay), but in England and Northern Ireland only certain EU citizens can vote in local elections: those from named countries, or those with continuous permission since 31 December 2020.

items.name: Voter Authority Certificate
items.text: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).
items.action: Replace the nationality list with the requirement to be registered to vote.
items.reason: Registered voters of other nationalities, such as eligible EU or foreign nationals in some elections, could wrongly be told they cannot apply.

problems.claim: Must be eligible to vote (registered on the electoral roll as a British, Irish, or qualifying Commonwealth citizen).
problems.note: Registration is required, but the text never ties this service to the listed nationalities (and the register page lets other nationalities register too).

items.name: Voter Authority Certificate
items.text: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.
items.action: Add that you can also apply if you no longer look like your photo ID or your name has changed, and say the certificate is only for voting in person.
items.reason: People whose photo ID no longer looks like them, or shows an old name, could be told they don't need a certificate and then be turned away at the polling station.

problems.claim: Must be registered to vote. Only needed if you do not already have an accepted form of photo ID.
problems.note: Registration is required, but the text gives other reasons to apply as well (you no longer look like your photo, or your name is different), and it applies only to voting in person.

items.name: Right to work check
items.text: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.
items.action: Reword to say the civil penalty applies when an illegal worker is employed, and that doing the check gives the employer a defence.
items.reason: Employers are told they get a penalty just for skipping the check, but the penalty only applies if they also employ someone without the right to work. This misstates the legal risk for some employers.

problems.claim: Required for all new employees before they begin work. Employer faces civil penalty if not done.
problems.note: The check before employment is stated, but the penalty only applies if the employer also employs an illegal worker, not simply for failing to do the check.

items.name: Right to work check
items.text: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.
items.action: Say the share code is one option, and list the other document or Employer Checking Service routes for non-UK/Irish nationals.
items.reason: Non-UK/Irish workers who cannot get a share code are wrongly told it is the only way to prove their right to work, so they and their employers may not find the right route.

problems.claim: Non-UK/Irish nationals provide a share code via the UK Visas & Immigration online portal. British/Irish citizens present their passport.
problems.note: Checking British/Irish passports and using share codes are both stated, but the text never says the online service is run by UK Visas and Immigration, and the share code is only one option.

items.name: Student Finance (tuition fee + maintenance loans)
items.text: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.
items.action: Change it to home in England plus 3 years' residence in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, and add Irish citizens.
items.reason: People who spent part of the 3 years elsewhere in the UK, and Irish citizens, could be wrongly told they don't qualify.

problems.claim: Must be normally resident in England for 3+ years before the course starts, and a UK national or settled person.
problems.note: The source requires your home to be in England and 3 years' residence in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, not 3 years in England specifically; it also includes Irish citizens.

items.name: File a confirmation statement
items.text: Must be a registered company, LLP or eligible UK business entity.
items.action: Cite the LLP confirmation statement guidance and replace 'eligible UK business entity' with the specific entity types that must file.
items.reason: Company directors and LLP members are covered correctly, but the vague 'eligible UK business entity' could make other kinds of business think they must file, or leave them unsure.

problems.claim: Must be a registered company, LLP or eligible UK business entity.
problems.note: The text says a company must file, but it never mentions LLPs or other eligible UK business entities, and it states no eligibility rule.

items.name: File annual accounts at Companies House
items.text: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.
items.action: Cite the Companies House guidance saying an officer or anyone with the authentication code, such as an accountant, can file.
items.reason: This tells directors and accountants who is allowed to file, which affects how they apply, but it is probably accurate and just needs a source.

problems.claim: Filed for a UK company by an officer, or by anyone with the company's authentication code such as an accountant. Limited liability partnerships can file only certain package accounts.
problems.note: The LLP restriction is stated, and the text says a password and authentication code are needed, but it never says the accounts can be filed by an officer or by anyone holding the authentication code, such as an accountant.

items.name: Appeal to Tax Tribunal
items.text: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.
items.action: Add appeals against Border Force, NCA, WRA and Gambling Commission decisions, and say direct tax appeals must go to HMRC first.
items.reason: People with decisions from these other bodies would wrongly be told they don't qualify, and 'usually' makes the required HMRC-first step for direct tax sound optional.

problems.claim: Must have an HMRC decision to appeal. Indirect tax decisions can usually go straight to the tribunal; direct tax decisions must usually be appealed to HMRC first.
problems.note: The direct/indirect routing is stated (the text says direct tax 'must' go to HMRC first, with no 'usually'), but the text does not require an HMRC decision: it also allows appeals against decisions by Border Force, the NCA, the WRA and the Gambling Commission.

items.name: Making Tax Digital enrolment
items.text: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.
items.action: Add the VAT exemptions and cite the MTD for Income Tax guidance for the 2026 phase-in.
items.reason: Businesses that qualify for an exemption would wrongly be told MTD is mandatory for them, and the income tax phase-in claim has no source.

problems.claim: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses. Phased in for income tax self-assessment from 2026.
problems.note: The VAT part is supported, apart from exemptions; the income tax self-assessment rollout from 2026 is not stated.

items.name: Short-term let licence (Scotland)
items.text: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.
items.action: Reword to cover anyone providing accommodation to guests on a short-term basis, not just owners or managers of residential property.
items.reason: The 'residential' and 'own or manage' conditions aren't in the sources and could wrongly tell some hosts, such as those letting non-residential or unusual accommodation, that they don't need a licence.

problems.claim: Must own or manage a residential property being let for short-term stays.
problems.note: The text links the licence to letting out accommodation to temporary guests, but it never says you must own or manage the property or that the property must be residential.

items.name: Street trading licence
items.text: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.
items.action: Cite the street trading legislation or council guidance that defines 'street' to include public places and covers goods or services.
items.reason: Traders in areas that are open to the public but are not streets, or who sell services, may be told a criterion applies to them based on wording the checked page does not state.

problems.claim: Selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales.
problems.note: The text covers trading in the street in England and Wales, but it never mentions a 'public place' or says 'goods or services'.

items.name: DBS check
items.text: Role involves working with children or vulnerable adults, or is otherwise in a specified list of eligible positions (healthcare, legal, financial services roles).
items.action: Cite the official DBS eligibility guidance for legal and financial services roles.
items.reason: People in legal or financial roles could be told wrongly whether they qualify for a more detailed check. These roles are probably eligible, but the checked pages don't say so.

problems.claim: Role involves working with children or vulnerable adults, or is otherwise in a specified list of eligible positions (healthcare, legal, financial services roles).
problems.note: The text mentions children, healthcare and specified positions, but does not mention legal or financial services roles.

items.name: Check and challenge business rates
items.text: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.
items.action: Add Wales and remove the unsourced requirement to occupy or own the property.
items.reason: People with property in Wales would wrongly be told they do not qualify, and anyone acting for a property they don't occupy or own could be turned away.

problems.claim: Must occupy or own a non-domestic property assessed for business rates in England.
problems.note: The text covers properties in England or Wales that have a rateable value for business rates and refers to 'your property', but it never says you must occupy or own the property, and it never limits the service to England or to non-domestic property.

items.name: Get a rod fishing licence
items.text: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.
items.action: Add the River Tweed exception to the England and Wales licence rule.
items.reason: People fishing the River Tweed would get the wrong answer about whether this licence applies there, though most anglers are not affected.

problems.claim: One licence covers England and Wales, including all of the Border Esk. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate arrangements.
problems.note: The text says a single England and Wales licence is needed, but it excludes the River Tweed, and the claim leaves that exception out.

items.name: Stamp Duty Land Tax return
items.text: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.
items.action: Change 'any purchase' to name the exemptions and describe additional properties as a 5% higher rate, not a different threshold.
items.reason: People buying additional properties could misunderstand how their tax is worked out, and exempt buyers would wrongly think the purchase is covered.

problems.claim: Any purchase of land or property in England (or Northern Ireland) — thresholds vary for first-time buyers, additional properties, etc.
problems.note: The text confirms England and Northern Ireland and a different threshold for first-time buyers, but for additional properties it describes a 5% higher rate rather than a different threshold, and it lists exemptions (for example freeholds under £40,000) where neither tax nor a return is needed, so not every purchase is covered.

items.name: Land Registry registration (AP1)
items.text: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.
items.action: Add the exemption for leases of 7 years or less.
items.reason: People taking short leases would be told wrongly that they must register.

problems.claim: Any purchase of land or property in England or Wales. Also required for remortgages, transfers of equity, and first-time registrations of unregistered land.
problems.note: The text covers buying, mortgaging, adding a joint owner and first registration, but 'any purchase' leaves out the short-lease exemption.

items.name: Sign your mortgage deed
items.text: Lender must participate in the Land Registry digital mortgage service.
items.action: Cite a page saying the homeowner's lender must use the digital mortgage service.
items.reason: It is a sensible reading of the pages and probably correct, but as an eligibility rule it decides who is told they can use the service, so it needs a source.

problems.claim: Lender must participate in the Land Registry digital mortgage service.
problems.note: The text says lenders can use HM Land Registry's digital mortgage service, but it never says the homeowner's lender must take part for the homeowner to be eligible.

items.name: First Homes / Help to Buy scheme
items.text: First-time buyer purchasing a new-build property through an eligible scheme. For First Homes: property must not exceed £250,000 after discount (£420,000 in London).
items.action: Change the wording so a First Homes property can be a new-build or a resale bought through an estate agent.
items.reason: People looking at a First Homes resale could wrongly be told they don't qualify, but most First Homes buyers buy new-builds, so the new-build rule is right for them.

problems.claim: First-time buyer purchasing a new-build property through an eligible scheme. For First Homes: property must not exceed £250,000 after discount (£420,000 in London).
problems.note: The first-time buyer rule and price caps are stated, but the text does not make new-build a requirement: First Homes can also be a resale bought through an estate agent.

items.name: Universal Credit
items.text: Must be habitually resident in the UK.
items.action: Cite the official guidance on the habitual residence test.
items.reason: The habitual residence test is real but mainly affects people who have recently arrived or returned to the UK, so it needs a source rather than a rewrite.

problems.claim: Must be habitually resident in the UK.
problems.note: The text requires living in the UK but does not mention a habitual residence test.

items.name: Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)
items.text: Must be classed as an employee (including agency workers) and have done some work for the employer; self-employed individuals are not eligible.
items.action: Change 'including agency workers' to say agency workers may be entitled.
items.reason: Agency workers could be told they definitely qualify when the official text says they only may be entitled.

problems.claim: Must be classed as an employee (including agency workers) and have done some work for the employer; self-employed individuals are not eligible.
problems.note: Being classed as an employee and having done some work are stated, and Source 2 says self-employed people lack employee rights. But agency workers only 'may be entitled', so the text does not say they are included outright.

items.name: Apply for bankruptcy
items.text: Must live or have a business in England or Wales.
items.action: Cite the residency rule and add that having lived or had a business in England or Wales in the last 3 years also qualifies.
items.reason: The residence test decides who can apply, and this wording may wrongly turn away people who have recently lived or traded in England or Wales but no longer do.

problems.claim: Must live or have a business in England or Wales.
problems.note: The text limits the service to England and Wales but does not say the applicant must live or have a business there.

items.name: Breathing Space (debt respite scheme)
items.text: Must engage with an FCA-authorised debt advice provider who applies on the person's behalf.
items.action: Cite the official source for which debt advice providers can apply, including any that are not FCA-authorised, such as local authorities.
items.reason: The requirement probably is accurate, but if other approved providers exist, some people could wrongly rule out an adviser who can in fact apply for them.

problems.claim: Must engage with an FCA-authorised debt advice provider who applies on the person's behalf.
problems.note: The text says a debt adviser applies on the person's behalf, but for Breathing Space it does not say the adviser must be FCA-authorised.

items.name: Debt Relief Order (DRO)
items.text: Must live or have been living in England or Wales.
items.action: Reword to 'must have lived or worked in England or Wales within the last 3 years'.
items.reason: Most applicants live in England or Wales now and aren't affected, but people who only worked there would be wrongly turned away, and people who lived there more than 3 years ago would be wrongly told they qualify.

problems.claim: Must live or have been living in England or Wales.
problems.note: The text requires living or working in England and Wales within the last 3 years; the claim leaves out both the working alternative and the 3-year time limit.

items.name: Send a fit note for an ESA claim
items.text: Must have a health condition or disability that prevents or limits work, evidenced by a fit note from a healthcare provider.
items.action: Say a fit note is needed only after more than 7 days off in a row, or when the person is told to send one.
items.reason: People off work for 7 days or fewer, or who have not been asked for a fit note, could be wrongly told they need one or that they do not qualify.

problems.claim: Must have a health condition or disability that prevents or limits work, evidenced by a fit note from a healthcare provider.
problems.note: The linked ESA page links a fit note to a disability or health condition that stops you working, but only when you have been off work for more than 7 days in a row, and the fit note page says you send one only when told to; the field states the fit note as a blanket requirement.

items.name: Healthy Start
items.text: England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland has Best Start Foods instead.
items.action: Cite an official page confirming Healthy Start covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
items.reason: The unsupported part says which nations the scheme covers, so if it were wrong, people in a nation left out or wrongly included would be told the wrong thing about whether they qualify.

problems.claim: England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland has Best Start Foods instead.
problems.note: The text says Scotland has Best Start Foods instead, but it never says the scheme covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

items.name: Update driving licence (name change)
items.text: Has legally changed name following marriage, civil partnership, deed poll or court order.
items.action: Cite a source that accepts court orders and legal name changes, or change the list to match the evidence the page names.
items.reason: People whose name changed another way could be wrongly told they do or do not qualify, but a typical married applicant is not affected.

problems.claim: Has legally changed name following marriage, civil partnership, deed poll or court order.
problems.note: Marriage, civil partnership and deed poll are listed as evidence, but a court order is not mentioned and no 'legal change' condition is stated.

items.name: Renew driving licence
items.text: Must hold a valid UK driving licence. Photo expiry renewal applies every 10 years for drivers under 70.
items.action: Replace the unstated 'valid UK licence' requirement with the stated ones: living in Great Britain and not being disqualified.
items.reason: Northern Ireland residents and disqualified drivers could be told wrongly that they qualify, and people whose photocard has already expired might wrongly think they cannot renew.

problems.claim: Must hold a valid UK driving licence. Photo expiry renewal applies every 10 years for drivers under 70.
problems.note: The 10-year renewal and the separate route for people 70 or over are stated, but the listed requirements are living in Great Britain and not being disqualified; holding a valid UK licence isn't stated as a requirement.

items.name: Marriage / CP certificate
items.text: Must have legally married or formed a civil partnership in England or Wales.
items.action: Add the exception that GRO also holds some marriage records from abroad, such as consular and armed forces registrations.
items.reason: People whose marriage abroad was registered with GRO could wrongly be told they can't get a certificate through this service.

problems.claim: Must have legally married or formed a civil partnership in England or Wales.
problems.note: The service covers certificates registered in England and Wales, but a linked page says GRO also holds some marriage records from abroad, so the text doesn't set a strict England-or-Wales requirement.

items.name: Marriage Allowance
items.text: One partner must have income below the Personal Allowance (£12,570/year). The other must be a basic-rate (20%) taxpayer.
items.action: Add that in Scotland the higher earner can pay starter, basic or intermediate rate.
items.reason: Scottish couples where the higher earner pays the intermediate rate could wrongly be told they don't qualify, though people elsewhere in the UK are not affected.

problems.claim: One partner must have income below the Personal Allowance (£12,570/year). The other must be a basic-rate (20%) taxpayer.
problems.note: The source supports the income limit and the basic-rate requirement, but it also allows starter or intermediate rate in Scotland, and the field leaves out that condition.

items.name: School place application
items.text: Local authority area determines which schools are offered. Catchment area, siblings, faith criteria vary by school.
items.action: Change the wording to say parents can apply for schools in other council areas through their own council, and cite a source for catchment areas or replace them with 'distance from the school'.
items.reason: Parents who live near a council boundary or want a school in another area could wrongly think they cannot apply for it and lose options, though most parents applying for local schools are not affected.

problems.claim: Local authority area determines which schools are offered. Catchment area, siblings, faith criteria vary by school.
problems.note: The text supports criteria varying by school, including siblings, faith and living close by, but it does not say the local authority area determines which schools are offered (you can apply for schools in other council areas), and it never mentions catchment areas.

items.name: Raise concerns about a school with Ofsted
items.text: Must have first completed the school's own complaints procedure before escalating to Ofsted.
items.action: Cite an official source for completing the full complaints procedure, or change the wording to 'already complained to the school and the problem is unresolved'.
items.reason: Some complainants may think they must wait until every stage of the school's procedure is finished before contacting Ofsted, which could delay them.

problems.claim: Must have first completed the school's own complaints procedure before escalating to Ofsted.
problems.note: The text says you must already have complained to the school and the problem is still unresolved, but it never says the school's full complaints procedure has to be completed first.

items.name: Provisional Driving Licence
items.text: Must be at least 15 years and 9 months old to apply. Must be 17 to drive on a public road (16 for a moped or light quad bike).
items.action: Cite the official driving-age rules and add the exceptions, such as age 16 for people getting the higher-rate mobility part of PIP.
items.reason: The ages 17 and 16 are generally correct, but the exceptions are left out, so some disabled applicants would get the wrong driving age.

problems.claim: Must be at least 15 years and 9 months old to apply. Must be 17 to drive on a public road (16 for a moped or light quad bike).
problems.note: The application age is stated, but the driving ages of 17 and 16 are not; the text only says the rules depend on age and vehicle.

items.name: Provisional Driving Licence
items.text: Must have been resident in Great Britain for at least 185 days in the last 12 months.
items.action: Remove 'in the last 12 months' and use the official wording about 185 days' permission to live in Great Britain.
items.reason: People who recently returned or arrived in Great Britain could be told wrongly that they don't qualify.

problems.claim: Must have been resident in Great Britain for at least 185 days in the last 12 months.
problems.note: The text gives 185 days of permission to live in Great Britain, but it does not mention 'the last 12 months'.

items.name: Provisional Driving Licence
items.text: Must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away (with glasses or contact lenses if worn). Certain medical conditions must be declared.
items.action: Cite the DVLA guidance on declaring notifiable medical conditions when applying.
items.reason: The duty to declare certain medical conditions is probably accurate but unsourced, and it affects what applicants with those conditions must do.

problems.claim: Must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away (with glasses or contact lenses if worn). Certain medical conditions must be declared.
problems.note: The number plate rule with glasses or contact lenses is stated, but the only declaration duty in the text covers certain eyesight problems, not medical conditions in general.

items.name: Make a SORN
items.text: Registered keeper of a vehicle whose tax has lapsed or is about to lapse, and which will be kept off public roads.
items.action: Remove the 'tax lapsed or about to lapse' condition and add the postal route for vehicles not yet registered in your name.
items.reason: People who have just bought a vehicle, or who want to make a SORN part-way through a tax period, could wrongly think they do not qualify or cannot apply.

problems.claim: Registered keeper of a vehicle whose tax has lapsed or is about to lapse, and which will be kept off public roads.
problems.note: The source ties online applications to vehicles registered in your name and covers off-road use, but it does not limit SORN to vehicles whose tax has lapsed or is about to. It allows applying in other months too, and the post route covers vehicles not registered in your name.

items.name: Tax your vehicle
items.text: Must have a V5C log book in your name (or the green new keeper slip if recently purchased), a valid MOT, and valid insurance before taxing.
items.action: Add the reminder letter reference route, say an MOT is only sometimes needed, and limit insurance evidence to Northern Ireland Post Office applications.
items.reason: People with only a reminder letter, or with vehicles that don't need an MOT, could be wrongly told they don't meet the criteria.

problems.claim: Must have a V5C log book in your name (or the green new keeper slip if recently purchased), a valid MOT, and valid insurance before taxing.
problems.note: The V5C or green slip is stated, but a reminder letter reference is also accepted, the MOT is only something you 'might' need, and insurance is only required in Northern Ireland.

items.name: Driving Test (practical)
items.text: A valid theory test pass certificate (valid for 2 years from the date of the theory test) is required to book.
items.action: Change the rule to a theory test pass within the last 2 years, cite that, and note that a lost certificate does not need replacing.
items.reason: Requiring the certificate itself could make people who lost it think they cannot book; the 2-year validity is probably stated on the theory test pages.

problems.claim: A valid theory test pass certificate (valid for 2 years from the date of the theory test) is required to book.
problems.note: You must have passed the theory test, but the source gives no 2-year validity and says you do not need a replacement certificate if you lose it.

items.name: National Careers Service
items.text: Free adviser-led guidance is available to adults in England. Scotland, Wales and NI have their own careers services.
items.action: Cite the source for England-only coverage and the separate services in the other nations, and change 'adults' to match the 13-or-over age range.
items.reason: Limiting guidance to adults could wrongly turn away 13 to 18 year olds, and the nation limits affect people outside England, though a typical adult in England would still get the right answer.

problems.claim: Free adviser-led guidance is available to adults in England. Scotland, Wales and NI have their own careers services.
problems.note: The text confirms you can get guidance from a careers adviser, but it does not say the service is free, for adults, or limited to England, and it does not mention separate services in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.

items.name: View and share driving licence
items.text: Must hold a UK driving licence.
items.action: Limit the criterion to licences issued in England, Wales or Scotland.
items.reason: Northern Ireland licence holders would wrongly be told they qualify for this service.

problems.claim: Must hold a UK driving licence.
problems.note: The text limits the service to licences issued in England, Wales or Scotland, which is narrower than any UK driving licence.

items.name: Emergency travel document
items.text: Must be outside the UK without a valid passport.
items.action: Replace 'without a valid passport' with the listed reasons for being unable to use your UK passport, including a full passport or one held by HM Passport Office or an embassy.
items.reason: People whose passport is still valid but is full or being held by HM Passport Office or an embassy could be wrongly told they do not qualify.

problems.claim: Must be outside the UK without a valid passport.
problems.note: The text requires being outside the UK and unable to use your UK passport for specific listed reasons, some of which (full, or held by HM Passport Office or an embassy) do not mean the passport is invalid, so 'without a valid passport' is only a loose match.

items.name: Appeal to Immigration Tribunal
items.text: Must have received a Home Office refusal that explicitly grants a right of appeal.
items.action: Reword to require a legal right of appeal, which is usually but not always stated in the decision letter, and cover revocation and deportation decisions as well as refusals.
items.reason: Most people's refusal letters do state their appeal right, but people appealing a revocation or deportation, or whose letter does not spell out the right, could wrongly be told they cannot appeal.

problems.claim: Must have received a Home Office refusal that explicitly grants a right of appeal.
problems.note: The text does require a legal right to appeal, but says you will only 'usually' be told about it in the decision letter, so it does not require the letter to grant the right explicitly; it also covers decisions other than refusals, such as revocation and deportation.

items.name: Maternity Allowance
items.text: Employment or self-employment evidence
items.action: Cite the MA1 guidance for self-employment evidence, or limit this to the employment details the form asks for.
items.reason: Self-employed claimants may gather evidence they are not asked for, or misunderstand what the form actually needs.

problems.claim: Employment or self-employment evidence is needed.
problems.note: The page asks for information about employment on the form and for payslips as proof of income, but it never asks for self-employment evidence as such.
problems.quote: You’ll need to give information about your employment in the 66 weeks before your baby is due

items.name: New Style Jobseeker's Allowance
items.text: CV and job-seeking evidence
items.action: Change to proof of job-seeking activity, and say a CV is only needed if the Claimant Commitment asks for one.
items.reason: Claimants may think they must bring a CV as evidence when only proof of job-seeking is required, which could worry or delay people who don't have one.

problems.claim: CV and job-seeking evidence is needed for this service.
problems.note: The text says you must show proof of job-seeking at regular appointments, but it mentions a CV only as something the Claimant Commitment might ask you to write, not as evidence you must provide.
problems.quote: you must show your work coach what you’ve been doing to look for work, for example proof of job applications and interviews

items.name: Divorce application (D8)
items.text: Marriage or civil partnership certificate
items.action: Limit this evidence item to the marriage certificate and send civil partners to the separate process for ending a civil partnership.
items.reason: Married applicants are unaffected, but civil partners could be led to think they use this divorce service instead of the separate process for ending a civil partnership.

problems.claim: You need a marriage or civil partnership certificate.
problems.note: The divorce page asks for a marriage certificate; civil partnership certificates belong to the separate process for ending a civil partnership.
problems.quote: your original marriage certificate or a certified copy (and a certified translation if it’s not in English)

items.name: Financial Consent Order
items.text: Draft consent order (D81 form)
items.action: Remove the D81 label from the draft consent order and list the D81 statement of information as a separate item.
items.reason: Calling the draft order 'D81' mixes up two separate documents, so some applicants may send one and leave out the other.

problems.claim: A draft consent order (D81 form) is needed.
problems.note: The text requires a signed draft consent order but never gives any form number such as D81.
problems.quote: draft a consent order sign the draft consent order - you also need 2 photocopies of the signed original

items.name: Financial Consent Order
items.text: Financial disclosure from both parties
items.action: Replace this with 'Statement of information form completed by both parties'.
items.reason: 'Financial disclosure' is vague, so some applicants may prepare the full Form E, which is only needed for contested cases, or miss the actual form that is required.

problems.claim: Financial disclosure from both parties is needed.
problems.note: Both parties must fill in a statement of information form, but the text does not call this financial disclosure or say what goes in it; the detailed financial statement (Form E) is only for the contested route.
problems.quote: fill in a statement of information form

items.name: Cancel Marriage Allowance
items.text: Government Gateway account or contact HMRC by phone
items.action: Replace the Government Gateway reference with proving identity using information HMRC holds, online or by phone through Marriage Allowance enquiries.
items.reason: People without a Government Gateway account may think they must set one up, or that they cannot cancel online, when the page only asks them to prove their identity using information HMRC holds.

problems.claim: Cancelling needs a Government Gateway account, or you can contact HMRC by phone.
problems.note: The text supports cancelling online or by phone through Marriage Allowance enquiries, but it never names Government Gateway. It only says you will prove your identity using information HMRC holds about you.
problems.quote: You must cancel online or by phone.

items.name: Statutory Maternity Pay
items.text: Written notice to employer of intended leave start date
items.action: Reword to say notice of the start date is required, and it only has to be in writing if the employer asks.
items.reason: Employees are told written notice is always required when it is only needed if the employer asks, which could confuse or delay someone who has already told their employer verbally.

problems.claim: You must give your employer written notice of the date you intend to start leave.
problems.note: The text requires notice of the start date, but it only has to be in writing if the employer asks for it.
problems.quote: You must give them at least 28 days' notice (in writing if they ask for it) and proof that you're pregnant.

items.name: Maternity exemption certificate (free prescriptions and dental)
items.text: Signed maternity exemption form from midwife or GP
items.action: Cite the official page describing the maternity exemption application form (FW8) that the health professional completes and signs, or reword it to say the professional completes the application.
items.reason: Pregnant women or new mothers may think they must get and hand in a signed paper form themselves, when the midwife or GP starts the application. The route is the same, but it could cause confusion or delay.

problems.claim: Signed maternity exemption form from midwife or GP
problems.note: The text says the professional completes the application, but it never mentions a signed form as evidence.
problems.quote: Speak to your midwife, doctor or health visitor. They'll complete the application for you.

items.name: Notify DVLA of medical condition
items.text: DVLA questionnaire (specific to condition)
items.action: Say that condition-specific forms are required for bus, coach and lorry licence holders, and that car and motorcycle drivers can report online.
items.reason: Car and motorcycle drivers may think they need a separate condition questionnaire when they can report online, though bus, coach and lorry drivers do need the form.

problems.claim: DVLA questionnaire (specific to condition)
problems.note: Condition-specific forms or questionnaires are stated, but as required only for bus, coach or lorry licence holders; car and motorcycle drivers can report online instead.
problems.quote: If you have a bus, coach or lorry licence, you’ll have to send a form or questionnaire to DVLA . There are different forms for different conditions and disabilities.

items.name: Renew driving licence at 70
items.text: Current driving licence
items.action: Reword so the current licence appears only as one example of photo ID, not a required item.
items.reason: People who have lost their licence, or whose licence has expired, could wrongly think they cannot renew, or that they must supply something the service does not require.

problems.claim: A current driving licence is needed.
problems.note: The text mentions a driving licence only as one example of photo ID for proving identity; it does not say a current licence must be provided.
problems.quote: This is to keep your details safe and usually involves using photo ID like a passport or driving licence.

items.name: Access to Work
items.text: Evidence of disability or health condition (may be required)
items.action: Reword to say you may be asked for more information about your condition and no diagnosis is needed.
items.reason: Some applicants may think they need medical evidence or a diagnosis before applying, which could put them off or delay them, though the 'may be required' wording softens this.

problems.claim: Evidence of disability or health condition may be required.
problems.note: The source says you may be asked for more information about your condition and that no diagnosis is needed to apply, but it never mentions providing evidence of the condition.
problems.quote: for more information about your work and your disability or health condition

items.name: Attendance Allowance
items.text: Terminally ill — claim using Special Rules immediately (DS1500/SR1 form)
items.action: Remove the DS1500 reference and 'immediately', and name only the SR1 form under the special rules for end of life.
items.reason: Terminally ill claimants or their clinicians could be pointed to the older DS1500 form, which SR1 has replaced, or given the wrong idea about timing, though the correct SR1 route is also named.

problems.claim: Terminally ill people can claim straight away under Special Rules using a DS1500/SR1 form.
problems.note: The text names form SR1 and 'special rules for end of life', but it does not mention DS1500 or say the claim is immediate; it only says 'more quickly'.
problems.quote: ask a medical professional for form SR1

items.name: Attendance Allowance
items.text: Under State Pension age — claim PIP instead.
items.action: Cite the PIP guidance for the under-State-Pension-age route and add that people in Scotland claim Adult Disability Payment instead.
items.reason: Pointing under-age people to PIP is probably right for most, but people in Scotland would be sent the wrong way.

problems.claim: People under State Pension age should claim PIP instead.
problems.note: The Attendance Allowance page requires State Pension age and the PIP page says new PIP claims are usually for people under that age, but neither page tells under-age people to claim PIP instead.
problems.quote: You also usually need to be under State Pension age to make a new PIP claim.

items.name: Mandatory Reconsideration
items.text: Decision letter from DWP
items.action: Change this to the date of the original decision rather than the letter as required evidence.
items.reason: Most people have their letter, but anyone who lost it could wrongly think they cannot ask for a reconsideration.

problems.claim: A decision letter from DWP is needed as evidence.
problems.note: The text refers to the decision letter and asks for the date of the original decision, but it does not require the letter as evidence and does not say DWP issues it.
problems.quote: If you do not have your decision letter, contact the office where you applied for the benefit.

items.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
items.text: Terminal illness — claim via Special Rules (faster decision, no assessment required)
items.action: Change 'no assessment required' to 'no face-to-face assessment'.
items.reason: People claiming under special rules could be surprised by a non-face-to-face assessment or contact they were told would not happen.

problems.claim: People with a terminal illness claim under Special Rules, which give a faster decision and need no assessment.
problems.note: The text supports special rules for end of life and says you get PIP more quickly, but it only rules out a face-to-face assessment, not every assessment.
problems.quote: You will not need to go to a face-to-face assessment.

items.name: UC Carer element
items.text: On Universal Credit and eligible for Carer's Allowance
items.action: Change the qualifier to being on Universal Credit and caring 35+ hours a week for someone who gets a listed benefit.
items.reason: Most people eligible for Carer's Allowance would also qualify, but framing it this way leaves out carers who meet the caring test and fail other Carer's Allowance conditions.

problems.claim: On Universal Credit and eligible for Carer's Allowance
problems.note: The source supports the element being added to Universal Credit. It frames the condition as caring for someone on a listed benefit, not as Carer's Allowance eligibility.
problems.quote: This is added to your Universal Credit if you care for someone who gets one of the following benefits:

items.name: Social Security & Child Support Tribunal
items.text: Mandatory Reconsideration Notice (SSCS1 form to appeal)
items.action: Say that SSCS1 is only for postal appeals outside Child Maintenance and Vaccine Damage Payment, and that a reason for not needing reconsideration can be given instead of the notice.
items.reason: People appealing online, people with Child Maintenance or Vaccine Damage Payment appeals, and people who do not need reconsideration could be sent to the wrong form or asked for a notice they do not have.

problems.claim: You need the Mandatory Reconsideration Notice, and form SSCS1 is used to appeal.
problems.note: The notice is required, but the text says SSCS1 is only for postal appeals (not Child Maintenance or Vaccine Damage Payment decisions), and that the reason for not needing a reconsideration can be given in place of the notice.
problems.quote: You’ll need to provide your mandatory reconsideration notice when applying.

items.name: Carer's Credit
items.text: Evidence of caring role (CA9176 form)
items.action: Cite the official Carer's Credit claim form page that gives the form number CA9176.
items.reason: Applicants looking for the claim form could search for the wrong document if the form number were wrong, though the Care Certificate requirement itself is supported.

problems.claim: Evidence of caring role is provided using the CA9176 form
problems.note: The text says the claim form includes a Care Certificate signed by a health or social care professional, but it never names a form 'CA9176'.
problems.quote: The form includes a Care Certificate - ask a health or social care professional to sign it for you.

items.name: Carer's Credit
items.text: Disability benefit details for the person cared for
items.action: Cite the claim form guidance showing that applicants must give details of the cared-for person's benefit.
items.reason: Applicants may be told to gather benefit details as evidence, and the pages do not confirm that the form asks for them.

problems.claim: Details of the disability benefit the person being cared for gets are needed as evidence
problems.note: The text requires the cared-for person to get one of the listed benefits, but it does not say the applicant has to give details of that benefit as evidence.
problems.quote: The person you’re looking after must get one of the following:

items.name: Blue Badge
items.text: PIP or DLA award letter
items.action: Make it conditional ('proof of benefits, if you get any') and cite the page that names award letters as accepted proof.
items.reason: Applicants who don't get PIP or DLA could think they need an award letter they don't have, though award letters are probably accepted proof for those who do get these benefits.

problems.claim: You need a PIP or DLA award letter as evidence.
problems.note: The text asks for proof of benefits only if you get any. It does not name a PIP or DLA award letter.

items.name: Marriage / CP certificate
items.text: Marriage took place — certificate issued at ceremony or ordered from register office
items.action: Remove the claim that a certificate is issued at the ceremony and say certificates are ordered from the register office or GRO.
items.reason: Recently married people may think they already have a certificate and not order one, then find they lack the document when they need it.

problems.claim: Marriage took place — certificate issued at ceremony or ordered from register office
problems.note: The text supports ordering from the register office, but it never says a certificate is issued at the ceremony.
problems.quote: You can also order certificates from the local register office where the birth, death or marriage was registered.

items.name: Passport name change
items.text: Current passport
items.action: Cite the official page that tells adults to send their current passport with a name-change application.
items.reason: Adults changing their name are told to send their current passport, which the adult page doesn't state, though the main passport application guidance very likely does.

problems.claim: Current passport is required evidence for a passport name change.
