problems.quote: You must send: the old passport a deed poll or similar document about the name change

items.name: Passport name change
items.text: New passport photos
items.action: Cite the passport photo guidance for adult name-change applications, and say whether online and postal applications need different photos.
items.reason: Adults may be told to get new photos on the checked pages' authority alone, which only mention photos for children applying by post, though every new passport application very likely needs a photo.

problems.claim: New passport photos are required for a passport name change.
problems.note: New photos are only required for child name-change applications made by post; the adult name-change page does not mention photos.
problems.quote: 2 new photos of your child if you apply by post

items.name: Free childcare — 30 hours (working parents)
items.text: Tax-Free Childcare account eligibility check (reconfirm every 3 months)
items.action: Rename this to reconfirming eligibility every 3 months through the childcare account shared by both schemes.
items.reason: Parents may think they need a separate Tax-Free Childcare account or check to keep their 30 hours, which could send them the wrong way, even though the 3-month reconfirmation itself is right.

problems.claim: A Tax-Free Childcare account eligibility check is needed, and eligibility must be reconfirmed every 3 months.
problems.note: The text supports reconfirming every 3 months through the childcare account, but it describes a shared childcare account for both schemes, not a Tax-Free Childcare account check; HMRC only checks Tax-Free Childcare eligibility at the same time as you apply.
problems.quote: You must sign in to your childcare account every 3 months to confirm you’re still eligible.

items.name: Free School Meals
items.text: Application via school office or local authority portal
items.action: Remove the school office route, or cite a source that supports it, and keep the local authority website as the way to apply.
items.reason: Some parents may try to apply at the school office when the official route is the council, which could delay their claim, but the correct route is also listed.

problems.claim: You apply through the school office or the local authority portal.
problems.note: Applying through the local authority's website is supported, but the text never mentions applying through the school office.
problems.quote: find out how to apply on your local authority’s website

items.name: SEND EHC plan assessment
items.text: School reports and educational assessments
items.action: Cite an official source for educational assessments as evidence, or change the wording to match the page (school reports and doctors' assessments).
items.reason: Parents could think they have to get educational assessments themselves before asking, when the page only mentions school reports and doctors' assessments.

problems.claim: School reports and educational assessments are used as evidence.
problems.note: The text mentions school reports and doctors' assessments, but it never mentions educational assessments.
problems.quote: any reports from your child’s school, nursery or childminder

items.name: SEND EHC plan assessment
items.text: Parental views (required to be included)
items.action: Cite the SEND regulations or code of practice on seeking parental views, or change 'required' to 'may be asked for'.
items.reason: Parents could believe their request fails without a written statement of their views, when the page only says they may be asked for a letter.

problems.claim: Parental views are required to be included.
problems.note: The text says you 'may be asked for' a letter from you about your child's needs, so it covers parental views but does not say they are required.
problems.quote: If they decide to carry out an assessment you may be asked for:

items.name: Provisional Driving Licence
items.text: UK passport or other acceptable identity document
items.action: Say that proof of identity may be needed and is usually photo ID such as a passport, not that a UK passport is always required.
items.reason: Some applicants would think they must provide a UK passport or other document when this is not always needed, or when other ID would do.

problems.claim: You need a UK passport or other acceptable identity document.
problems.note: The text says proving your identity may be needed and usually uses photo ID like a passport, but it does not say this is always required and does not specify a UK passport.
problems.quote: You’ll be told when you sign in if you need to prove your identity. This is to keep your details safe and usually involves using photo ID like a passport.

items.name: Tax your vehicle
items.text: V5C held in keeper's name, valid MOT and insurance in place
items.action: Cite the rules on when an MOT is needed and on insurance, or reword so MOT and insurance aren't presented as universal conditions for taxing.
items.reason: Vehicles that don't need an MOT, and people with a reminder letter instead of a V5C, may be wrongly treated as not qualifying.

problems.claim: The V5C is held in the keeper's name, and a valid MOT and insurance are in place.
problems.note: The V5C in your name is stated, but the MOT is only something you 'might' need, and insurance is only required in Northern Ireland.
problems.quote: your vehicle log book (V5C) (it must be in your name)

items.name: Tax your vehicle
items.text: Valid MOT certificate (most vehicles)
items.action: Say MOT evidence is only sometimes needed, that a screenshot of the MOT history is accepted, and cite the rule on which vehicles need an MOT.
items.reason: Some people may think they must produce a paper MOT certificate when a screenshot is accepted or no MOT evidence is needed at all.

problems.claim: You need a valid MOT certificate (most vehicles).
problems.note: MOT evidence 'might' be needed, and a screenshot of the MOT history is accepted instead of a certificate; the text does not say 'most vehicles'.
problems.quote: For example, a screenshot of your vehicle’s MOT history or your MOT certificate, if you have one.

items.name: Driving Test (practical)
items.text: Provisional driving licence photocard
items.action: Add that a passport together with a paper licence is accepted in place of a photocard.
items.reason: Most people have a photocard, but anyone with an old paper licence could wrongly think they cannot attend.

problems.claim: You need a provisional driving licence photocard.
problems.note: The source asks for your UK driving licence and allows a passport with a paper licence instead of a photocard; it does not specifically say a provisional photocard.
problems.quote: your UK driving licence

items.name: Tax credits (ended April 2025)
items.text: New claimants must use Universal Credit — Tax Credits is closed to new applications
items.action: Say new claimants may be able to get Universal Credit or Pension Credit, instead of saying they must use Universal Credit.
items.reason: People over State Pension age could be sent to Universal Credit when Pension Credit is the right route for them, but most working-age people would still be pointed the right way.

problems.claim: Tax credits are closed to new applications and new claimants must use Universal Credit.
problems.note: The page supports that new claims are closed, but it says people may be able to get Universal Credit or Pension Credit, not that new claimants must use Universal Credit.
problems.quote: You cannot make a new claim for Child Tax Credit or Working Tax Credit. You may be able to get Universal Credit or Pension Credit instead.

items.name: Child performance licence
items.text: Chaperone supervision arrangements
items.action: Cite a page that requires chaperone details with the application, or say they are needed only when a chaperone is required.
items.reason: Some applicants might be told to provide chaperone arrangements as evidence when their case doesn't need a chaperone or the application doesn't ask for them.

problems.claim: Chaperone supervision arrangements are evidence needed for the application.
problems.note: The text requires chaperone supervision in some cases but does not say the arrangements must be provided as evidence with the application.
problems.quote: If the child will not be with their parent, school teacher or home tutor, they must be supervised by a chaperone approved by the council.

items.name: House-to-house collection licence
items.text: Application to local council (free)
items.action: Add the London exception: apply to the Metropolitan Police there, not the local council.
items.reason: London applicants would send their application to the wrong body, while applicants elsewhere are correctly told to apply to the council for free.

problems.claim: Application to local council (free)
problems.note: The text supports applying to the council for free, but says that in London you apply to the Metropolitan Police instead.
problems.quote: Contact your council (or if you are in London, the Metropolitan Police) to apply for the licence.

items.name: New Style Jobseeker's Allowance
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone.
items.action: Cite the official page that gives the Jobcentre Plus phone route for applying, or change the wording to 'contact Jobcentre Plus'.
items.reason: People who can't apply online could be sent to the wrong number, such as the change-of-circumstances helpline, if the phone route for applying isn't sourced properly.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this by phone.
problems.note: The text says you can apply another way by contacting Jobcentre Plus but does not say this is by phone; the only phone number given is the helpline for reporting changes, not for applying.
problems.quote: You need to either: contact Jobcentre Plus if you live in England, Scotland or Wales

items.name: Maternity exemption certificate (free prescriptions and dental)
items.text: You can apply or do this in person.
items.action: Reword it to say you apply by asking your midwife, doctor or health visitor, and remove the unsupported 'in person' requirement.
items.reason: Applicants may think they must visit somewhere in person, or not realise the application goes through their health professional. That could send some of them the wrong way or put them off applying.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this in person.
problems.note: You apply by speaking to your health professional, but the text does not say this has to be face to face.
problems.quote: Speak to your midwife, doctor or health visitor. They'll complete the application for you.

items.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone. You can apply or do this by post.
items.action: Say the full application can be made online only in some areas, and describe the phone and post routes correctly.
items.reason: People outside the online areas could be sent to an online route that is not available to them.

problems.claim: You can apply online.
problems.note: The text says the full application can be made online only in some areas.
problems.quote: You can make your full application online in some areas.

items.name: Free prescriptions (disability)
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by post.
items.action: Separate the routes: say a PPC can be bought online, and a medical exemption certificate is applied for through your GP using form FP92A.
items.reason: People applying for a medical exemption could be sent to an online or post route that doesn't exist, instead of being told to go through their GP.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this online.
problems.note: The text says you can buy a PPC online and check eligibility on the NHSBSA website, but not that you can apply online for free prescriptions.
problems.quote: You can buy an NHS prescription prepayment certificate online .

problems.claim: You can apply or do this by post.
problems.note: The only mention of post is receiving PPC details by post; the text never says you can apply by post.

items.name: Inherited State Pension (Additional or extra)
items.text: You can apply or do this by phone.
items.action: Cite the Pension Service contact route for claiming inherited State Pension instead of the general State Pension phone-claim rule.
items.reason: The phone rule quoted is for general State Pension claims within 4 months of State Pension age, so some survivors could be given the wrong claim route or condition, although inheritance is probably arranged by contacting the Pension Service.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this by phone.
problems.note: Phone claims are allowed only if you will reach State Pension age in the next 4 months, and the text is about claiming the State Pension in general, not this inheritance specifically.
problems.quote: If you’ll reach State Pension age in the next 4 months, you can phone the Pension Service to claim.

items.name: Check & top up NI record
items.text: Applying online needs a Government Gateway user ID (sign-in)
items.action: Cite the source that names the sign-in account, or list every accepted sign-in method.
items.reason: Naming only Government Gateway could send people who use another accepted sign-in the wrong way, or put them off applying online.

problems.claim: Applying online needs a Government Gateway user ID (sign-in).
problems.note: The text says a sign-in is needed, but it does not say which account; Government Gateway is not named.
problems.quote: You’ll need to sign in to check your National Insurance record. If you do not already have sign in details, you’ll be able to create them.

items.name: Income tax on pension
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone.
items.action: Cite HMRC's Income Tax helpline page for the phone route, or remove the phone claim.
items.reason: People who want to query or fix tax on their pension could be sent to a phone route the pages don't confirm, though HMRC's general Income Tax helpline probably handles these queries.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this by phone.
problems.note: The service page says to contact HMRC but never mentions phone; the phone routes on the linked pages are for other services (Self Assessment forms and State Pension claims).

items.name: Sign up for flood warnings
items.text: No account or sign-in is needed to apply
items.action: Say that no existing sign-in is needed, but signing up creates an account you sign in to for later changes.
items.reason: New sign-ups get the right answer, but people who want to update or cancel their warnings would wrongly be told there is no account to sign in to.

problems.claim: No account or sign-in is needed to apply.
problems.note: The text asks for no existing sign-in to sign up for the first time (just an email address), but signing up creates an account, and you sign in to it to make later changes.
problems.quote: Sign in to your account to: update your details remove warnings for an area delete your account

items.name: NHS Low Income Scheme (HC2/HC3)
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by post.
items.action: Cite the NHSBSA page on applying with a paper HC1 form
items.reason: Postal applications using an HC1 form do exist, but the cited page doesn't support this, so people who can't apply online could be given unclear or unsupported instructions.

problems.claim: You can apply by post.
problems.note: The page links to another page on how to apply if you cannot apply online, but never says you can apply by post; the postal address given is only for asking for a review.

items.name: Best Start Foods
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone.
items.action: Cite the Social Security Scotland page that confirms you can apply by phone.
items.reason: People could be sent to phone to apply when the sourced number is only for enquiries and bank details. Phone applications are probably allowed, though, and online is still a valid route.

problems.claim: You can apply by phone.
problems.note: The phone number is given for enquiries and for bank details, not for applying.

items.name: Marriage / CP certificate
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by post. You can apply or do this in person.
items.action: Cite a source confirming in-person ordering at register offices, or change the wording to ordering from the local register office.
items.reason: Some people may turn up at a register office expecting to order over the counter where that service isn't offered.

problems.claim: You can apply or do this in person.
problems.note: The text says you can order from a local register office, but it never says this is done in person.
problems.quote: You can also order certificates from the local register office where the birth, death or marriage was registered.

items.name: Driving Test (practical)
items.text: You can apply or do this online. You can apply or do this by phone.
items.action: Cite the DVSA page on booking by phone, or limit phone booking to upgrade tests.
items.reason: Most people book online, but some may be sent to a phone route the source only describes for upgrade tests.

problems.claim: You can apply by phone.
problems.note: Phone booking is only described for upgrade tests, not for booking in general.
problems.quote: You must call the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency ( DVSA ) if you need an ‘upgrade’ test

items.name: Check and pay Clean Air Zone charges
items.text: No account or sign-in is needed to apply
items.action: Change the wording to say businesses checking several vehicles need an account, while single-vehicle users do not.
items.reason: Business users managing several vehicles would be wrongly told they need no account, though individual drivers are unaffected.

problems.claim: No account or sign-in is needed to apply.
problems.note: The text names no account for a single vehicle, but it says businesses checking several vehicles need an account, so the claim does not hold for every user.
problems.quote: If you're a business and want to check a number of vehicles you'll need: an account - you can create one when you use this service

items.name: Criminal Injuries Compensation
items.text: No account or sign-in is needed to apply
items.action: Add that you need a GOV.UK One Login to save your application and come back to it later.
items.reason: Applicants who can't finish in one go wouldn't know they need a One Login to save their progress, and could lose their work.

problems.claim: No account or sign-in is needed to apply
problems.note: The text suggests you need a GOV.UK One Login only if you want to save your application and come back to it later, but it never says outright that no account is needed, and the claim leaves out the One Login condition.
problems.quote: You’ll need a GOV.UK One Login if you want to save your application and return to it later.

items.name: Request a baby loss certificate
items.text: Available to parents who experienced the loss of a baby before 24 weeks gestation (including miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy). Free and optional. The certificate is not a legal document (it cannot be used to claim benefits) and is not added to the GP record. Losses before 1 October 1992 are covered up to 28 weeks. England only; arrives by post within 21 days.
items.action: Cite the official baby loss certificate guidance confirming that miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy are included.
items.reason: If this example is wrong, people who had a miscarriage or an ectopic pregnancy could be told wrongly that they qualify. The main 24-week rule is still supported for everyone else.

problems.claim: This includes miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy.
problems.note: The text never mentions miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy.

items.name: Child Maintenance Service
items.text: A statutory service for parents who cannot reach a private maintenance arrangement. CMS calculates payments based on the paying parent's income. A fee applies to use the Collect & Pay service.
items.action: Cite official sources for the income-based calculation and the Collect & Pay fees, and make clear that parents don't have to fail to agree before they can use the CMS.
items.reason: The statutory, income-based and fee claims are accurate and shown elsewhere, but the 'cannot reach an arrangement' wording could lead some parents to wrongly think they aren't eligible, and the fee mention gives no amounts or details of who pays.

problems.claim: The CMS is a statutory service.
problems.note: The text does not describe the service as statutory.

problems.claim: It is for parents who cannot reach a private maintenance arrangement.
problems.note: The CMS is presented as an alternative to a private arrangement, but the text does not limit it to parents who cannot reach one.
problems.quote: privately between parents , if both parents agree through the Child Maintenance Service

problems.claim: CMS calculates payments based on the paying parent's income.
problems.note: The text says the CMS works out an amount but does not mention income as the basis.
problems.quote: work out an amount to pay

problems.claim: A fee applies to use the Collect & Pay service.
problems.note: The text does not mention fees or Collect & Pay.

items.name: Register the birth
items.text: Required for every birth. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland it must be registered within 42 days; in Scotland within 21 days (different process). Usually done by a parent; others can register if the parents cannot.
items.action: Cite the Scottish registration guidance for the 21-day deadline and the requirement to register every birth, or limit the statement to England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
items.reason: Only parents registering in Scotland depend on the unsourced 21-day deadline and the 'every birth' scope; for most users in England, Wales and Northern Ireland the 42-day rule is correct.

problems.claim: Every birth must be registered.
problems.note: The source only says this for births in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, not for every birth.
problems.quote: All births in England, Wales and Northern Ireland must be registered within 42 days of the child being born.

problems.claim: In Scotland a birth must be registered within 21 days.
problems.note: The source gives no deadline for Scotland.

items.name: Divorce application (D8)
items.text: No-fault divorce since April 2022 — no reasons needed. Apply online or on paper. Minimum timescale: 20 weeks to apply for the conditional order, then at least 43 days before applying for the final order. Fee £628. Can apply jointly or individually.
items.action: Cite the official page that says divorce has been no-fault since 6 April 2022 and needs no reason.
items.reason: Applicants depend on this to know whether they must give a reason, so an unsupported claim here affects what they do, although it is very likely accurate.

problems.claim: Divorce has been no-fault since April 2022 and no reasons are needed.
problems.note: The text refers to applications issued before and after 6 April 2022, and to reasons only for older cases, but it never says divorce is no-fault or that no reasons are needed.

items.name: Employment Tribunal claim
items.text: Anyone can make a claim to an Employment Tribunal for a qualifying employment rights violation. Must have gone through Acas early conciliation first (in most cases). Time limit is 3 months minus 1 day from the act complained of.
items.action: Replace 'anyone' with the actual condition, mention the separate Northern Ireland route, say Acas must be notified rather than conciliation completed, and cite a source for 'minus 1 day'.
items.reason: Most claimants would still act correctly, but people in Northern Ireland are sent the wrong way, and anyone who thinks conciliation is required, or who counts unfair dismissal time from the wrong date, could be misled.

problems.claim: Anyone can make a claim to an Employment Tribunal for a qualifying employment rights violation.
problems.note: The text says you can claim if you think you were treated unlawfully, but it never says 'anyone', and it notes a different way to claim in Northern Ireland.
problems.quote: You can make a claim to an employment tribunal if you think someone has treated you unlawfully, such as your employer, a potential employer or a trade union.

problems.claim: In most cases you must have gone through Acas early conciliation before claiming.
problems.note: The text says you must notify Acas and will usually need a certificate, but you can choose not to take part in conciliation, so going through it is not required.
problems.quote: If early conciliation does not work or you choose not to take part, Acas will send you an early conciliation certificate.

problems.claim: The time limit is 3 months minus 1 day from the act complained of.
problems.note: The text gives 3 months but does not mention 'minus 1 day', and for unfair dismissal the period starts when employment ended.
problems.quote: You usually have to make a claim within 3 months of your employment ending or the problem happening.

items.name: Legal Aid application
items.text: Government funding for legal advice and representation in certain cases. Both means-tested (income/capital) and merits-tested (strength of case). Domestic abuse cases have wider automatic eligibility. Applied via a legal aid solicitor.
items.action: Replace 'automatic eligibility' with 'may still qualify above the limits', and cite a source for the merits test.
items.reason: Domestic abuse victims could think they qualify automatically when they may still need to pass the other tests. The strength-of-case point is probably true elsewhere.

problems.claim: Legal aid is merits tested on the strength of the case.
problems.note: The text never mentions judging the strength of the case.

problems.claim: Domestic abuse cases have wider automatic eligibility.
problems.note: The text says domestic abuse cases may still qualify above the limits, but it does not say eligibility is automatic.
problems.quote: You might still be eligible if you have a higher income and your case is about: domestic abuse

items.name: Child Benefit transfer
items.text: After separation, only one parent can claim Child Benefit per child. If the child's living arrangements change, Child Benefit must be transferred to the main carer.
items.action: Replace 'must be transferred to the main carer' with the official rule that the person the child now lives with makes a new claim, and that priority rules decide between two claimants.
items.reason: Parents in shared care, or a claimant who still pays towards the child, could wrongly be told they must give up the benefit, and people may expect a transfer instead of making a new claim.

problems.claim: If the child's living arrangements change, Child Benefit must be transferred to the main carer.
problems.note: The text describes changing who gets Child Benefit when you want someone else to claim, but it never says the benefit must be transferred to the main carer when living arrangements change.
problems.quote: Contact the Child Benefit Office if you want someone else to claim Child Benefit, for example, your spouse or partner. After you've done this, tell the other person to make a new claim.

items.name: Tax-Free Childcare account
items.text: For every £8 a parent pays into their account, the government adds £2 (up to £500 per child per quarter, or £1,000 if disabled). Must be in work and earning at least NMW for 16 hours.
items.action: Change 'must' to 'usually' and add the exception for a non-working partner who gets certain benefits.
items.reason: Couples where one partner doesn't work but gets qualifying benefits (for example Carer's Allowance or incapacity benefits) would wrongly be told they don't qualify.

problems.claim: The parent must be in work.
problems.note: The text says 'usually' and gives exceptions, such as a non-working parent whose partner works and who gets certain benefits, so 'must' goes further than the text.
problems.quote: You’ll usually need to be working (or returning to work)

items.name: Statutory Redundancy Pay
items.text: A legal entitlement for employees made compulsorily redundant after 2 or more years of continuous employment. Amount depends on age, weekly pay (capped at £751/week for redundancies on or after 6 April 2026, maximum £22,530 total), and length of service. Employer must pay — Employment Tribunal if they refuse.
items.action: Remove the word "compulsorily" and add that laid-off or short-time workers can also qualify.
items.reason: Employees who are laid off or put on short-time working, and possibly people who took voluntary redundancy, could wrongly think they cannot get redundancy pay.

problems.claim: It is a legal entitlement for employees made compulsorily redundant after 2 or more years of continuous employment.
problems.note: The text supports employees with 2 or more years' continuous service, but it does not limit the entitlement to compulsory redundancy: staff who are laid off or put on short-time working can also qualify.
problems.quote: have been dismissed, laid off or put on short-time working - those who opted for early retirement do not qualify

items.name: Renew driving licence at 70
items.text: All driving licences expire at age 70 and must be renewed every 3 years thereafter. Renewal is free online (or via D46P form, 3-week processing). Applicant must self-declare they meet minimum eyesight standards and have no condition preventing them from driving. Driving on an expired licence is unlawful.
items.action: Cite the official pages for expiry at 70, the self-declaration, and it being unlawful to drive on an expired licence.
items.reason: People renewing rely on the expiry date and the declaration step to get the deadline and the required actions right; these are probably correct but are not backed by the checked text.

problems.claim: All driving licences expire at age 70.
problems.note: The text implies that renewal is due at 70, but it never says that all licences expire at 70.
problems.quote: DVLA will automatically send you this form 90 days before your 70th birthday or before your licence expires.

problems.claim: The applicant must self-declare that they meet minimum eyesight standards and have no condition preventing them from driving.
problems.note: The text lists these as conditions for using the service, but it does not describe them as a self-declaration.
problems.quote: you meet the minimum eyesight requirement you are not prevented from driving for any reason

problems.claim: Driving on an expired licence is unlawful.
problems.note: The text does not address driving on an expired licence.

items.name: Repay a benefit overpayment
items.text: Applies to anyone who has received more benefit than they were entitled to and has been notified of an overpayment by DWP. Repayments are typically deducted automatically from ongoing benefits.
items.action: Add that tax credits, Child Benefit, Social Security Scotland and Department for Communities overpayments follow separate processes.
items.reason: People overpaid tax credits, Child Benefit or Scottish or Northern Irish benefits could be sent into the DWP process when their case is handled elsewhere.

problems.claim: This applies to anyone who has received more benefit than they were entitled to and has been told about the overpayment by DWP.
problems.note: The text covers people who were overpaid and sent a letter. But it doesn't cover everyone: tax credits, Child Benefit, Social Security Scotland and DfC overpayments follow a different process.
problems.quote: You’ll get a letter to let you know that you’ve been overpaid.

items.name: Disability Living Allowance (Child)
items.text: For children under 16 with a disability or health condition that means they need extra looking after or have difficulty walking. Not means-tested. Replaced by Child Disability Payment in Scotland.
items.action: Cite an official DLA source saying income and savings do not affect DLA, not the PIP page.
items.reason: Families deciding whether it is worth claiming rely on the 'not means-tested' claim. It is probably true, but the DLA page only says you can claim in or out of work.

problems.claim: DLA for children is not means-tested.
problems.note: The DLA page says only that you can claim whether you are in or out of work; it never says income or savings are ignored (the PIP page says that about PIP, a different benefit).

items.name: Mandatory Reconsideration
items.text: If you disagree with a DWP decision on Universal Credit, JSA, ESA, PIP, or other benefits, you must request a Mandatory Reconsideration before you can appeal to a tribunal. Must be requested within 1 month of the decision letter.
items.action: Add the exception for decisions that can go straight to an appeal, and cite a source that names DWP.
items.reason: The absolute 'must' misleads people whose decision can be appealed directly. The DWP wording is background only.

problems.claim: If you disagree with a DWP decision on Universal Credit, JSA, ESA, PIP or other benefits, you can request a Mandatory Reconsideration.
problems.note: The listed benefits include ESA, JSA, PIP and Universal Credit, but the text never calls these DWP decisions.
problems.quote: You can ask for mandatory reconsideration for benefits including:

problems.claim: You must request a Mandatory Reconsideration before you can appeal to a tribunal.
problems.note: The text says you cannot appeal until you get the notice, but also that some decisions can go straight to an appeal.
problems.quote: Some decisions cannot be reconsidered. Others can go straight to an appeal .

items.name: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
items.text: For people aged 16 to 64 with a long-term health condition or disability. Not means-tested. Has daily living and mobility components, each at standard or enhanced rate. Opens access to many other benefits.
items.action: Replace '16 to 64' with '16 or over and under State Pension age'.
items.reason: A fixed upper age of 64 would wrongly exclude people who are 65 or older but still under State Pension age.

problems.claim: PIP is for people aged 16 to 64 with a long-term health condition or disability.
problems.note: The text gives 16 or over and under State Pension age, but it never gives 64 as the upper age.
problems.quote: Personal Independence Payment ( PIP ) is a tax-free benefit for people aged 16 or over who have not reached State Pension age .

items.name: Council Tax Disability Reduction
items.text: Council Tax bill is reduced to the next band down if the property has certain features essential for a disabled resident: a room used mainly by the disabled person, an extra bathroom or kitchen, or extra space for wheelchair use.
items.action: Cite the council tax reduction regulations or council guidance for the 'used mainly by the disabled person' condition.
items.reason: The 'mainly used' condition is probably accurate, since the regulations say 'predominantly', but it adds a qualifying test the page doesn't state, which could affect people whose room is shared or used for more than one thing.

problems.claim: One qualifying feature is a room used mainly by the disabled person.
problems.note: The text mentions an 'other room that you need for the disabled person' but does not say the room must be used mainly by that person.
problems.quote: an extra bathroom, kitchen or other room that you need for the disabled person

items.name: Disabled Facilities Grant
items.text: Up to £30,000 (England) towards adaptations to help a disabled person live independently at home: ramps, stairlifts, wider doorways, accessible bathrooms. Means-tested for applicants over 18. Occupational Therapist assessment required.
items.action: Say landlords are also exempt from the means test and the council may send an occupational therapist or trained assessor, rather than saying an OT assessment is required.
items.reason: Landlord applicants would wrongly expect a means test, and applicants may think they must arrange an OT assessment when the council handles any assessment.

problems.claim: Examples include accessible bathrooms.
problems.note: The text mentions a level access shower but not accessible bathrooms in general.
problems.quote: level access shower

problems.claim: The means test applies to applicants over 18.
problems.note: Only the under-18 exemption is stated. Landlords are also exempt from the income test, so it does not apply to all adult applicants.
problems.quote: Disabled children under 18 can get a grant without their parents’ income being taken into account.

problems.claim: An Occupational Therapist assessment is required.
problems.note: The text says the council 'may' send an occupational therapist or a trained assessor. It does not say an OT assessment is required.
problems.quote: The council may send an occupational therapist or trained assessor to see you.

items.name: NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC)
items.text: Available to adults assessed as having a primary health need that is complex, intense, or unpredictable. Eligibility is assessed by a multidisciplinary team using the NHS Continuing Healthcare Decision Support Tool. Available to people aged 18 or over, in any setting.
items.action: Cite the National Framework and the Decision Support Tool guidance for the need characteristics, the multidisciplinary team assessment and the any-setting statement.
items.reason: Applicants whose needs they would not call 'complex, intense or unpredictable' might wrongly decide they don't qualify, although these terms and the assessment process are probably stated in the framework.

problems.claim: Available to adults assessed as having a primary health need that is complex, intense or unpredictable.
problems.note: The text mentions a primary health need, but it does not use the words complex, intense or unpredictable.
problems.quote: where an individual is found to have a primary health need

problems.claim: Eligibility is assessed by a multidisciplinary team using the NHS Continuing Healthcare Decision Support Tool.
problems.note: The text says the framework sets out the processes for deciding eligibility, but it does not name a multidisciplinary team or the Decision Support Tool.

problems.claim: Available to people aged 18 or over, in any setting.
problems.note: The text states the age of 18 or over, but it does not say the care is available in any setting.
problems.quote: Such care is provided to an individual aged 18 or over

items.name: Motability scheme
items.text: Lease a car, powered wheelchair or scooter by using the Enhanced Rate of the Mobility Component of PIP. The allowance is paid directly to Motability. No credit check required.
items.action: Cite the Motability scheme pages for the vehicle types, direct payment and no credit check, and name all qualifying allowances.
items.reason: Payment direct to Motability and no credit check are probably accurate, but naming only PIP could wrongly suggest that DLA, AFIP, WPMS or Scottish disability payment recipients do not qualify.

problems.claim: You can lease a car, powered wheelchair or scooter by using the Enhanced Rate of the Mobility Component of PIP.
problems.note: The text supports leasing a vehicle with a qualifying mobility allowance, but it does not mention powered wheelchairs, scooters, PIP or the Enhanced Rate.
problems.quote: Use your qualifying mobility allowance to lease a brand-new vehicle.

problems.claim: The allowance is paid directly to Motability.
problems.note: The text does not say how or to whom the allowance is paid.

problems.claim: No credit check is required.
problems.note: The text does not mention credit checks.

items.name: Child Winter Heating Payment
items.text: Annual payment of £265.50 for children in Scotland who receive the highest rate of the care component of Child Disability Payment (or DLA). Paid automatically — no application required.
items.action: Cite the official eligibility criteria and add the Adult Disability Payment and PIP route for young people and the minority who must apply.
items.reason: Most families on the highest care rate are described correctly, but young people who qualify through other disability benefits, and people who must apply, could be wrongly told they do not qualify or need not act.

problems.claim: It is for children in Scotland who get the highest rate of the care component of Child Disability Payment (or DLA).
problems.note: The text never says what the eligibility criteria are.

problems.claim: It is paid automatically and no application is required.
problems.note: The text says most people do not need to apply, not that no one does.
problems.quote: Most people do not need to apply. You’ll get this payment automatically if you qualify.

items.name: Lasting Power of Attorney
items.text: A legal document appointing trusted people (attorneys) to make decisions on your behalf. Two types: Property & Financial Affairs (can be used immediately), and Health & Welfare (only if you lose capacity). Must be registered with OPG before use.
items.action: Replace 'can be used immediately' with 'can be used once registered, with the donor's permission'.
items.reason: Attorneys for property and finance might act without the donor's permission while the donor still has capacity, thinking 'immediately' means no conditions apply.

problems.claim: A Property & Financial Affairs LPA can be used immediately.
problems.note: The text says it can be used once it is registered and with the donor's permission; 'immediately' leaves out both conditions.
problems.quote: It can be used as soon as it’s registered, with your permission.

items.name: SR1 form (Special Rules for terminal illness)
items.text: Available where a clinician (GP, consultant, specialist nurse) confirms a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The form is completed by the clinician, not the patient.
items.action: Reword to the official test: the clinician would not be surprised if the patient died within 12 months.
items.reason: Saying a clinician must 'confirm' a prognosis may put off patients whose clinician cannot give a firm life expectancy but would still sign the form.

problems.claim: The life expectancy is 12 months or less.
problems.note: The text says 'less than 12 months', not '12 months or less', and frames it as the clinician not being surprised.
problems.quote: you would not be surprised if they were to live for less than 12 months

items.name: Housing Benefit
items.text: Housing Benefit helps pension-age tenants on low income pay rent. Working-age claimants should apply for Universal Credit instead. Claimed through local council, not DWP directly. Backdatable up to 3 months.
items.action: Add the supported, sheltered and temporary housing exception for working-age claimants, add the Pension Service route through a Pension Credit claim, and remove 'not DWP directly'.
items.reason: Working-age people in supported housing would be sent to Universal Credit by mistake, and pension-age people claiming Pension Credit wouldn't be told they can claim through the Pension Service.

problems.claim: Working-age claimants should apply for Universal Credit instead.
problems.note: The text points people who are not eligible to Universal Credit, but working-age people in supported, sheltered or temporary housing can still make a new Housing Benefit claim.
problems.quote: Most people will need to claim Universal Credit instead .

problems.claim: It is claimed through the local council, not directly through DWP.
problems.note: The council route is stated, but the text also gives a route through a Pension Credit claim with the Pension Service, and it never mentions DWP.
problems.quote: You can either apply: through your local council as part of a Pension Credit claim, if you’re eligible for this

problems.claim: It can be backdated by up to 3 months.
problems.note: The text says backdating may be possible but gives no 3-month limit.
problems.quote: You might also be able to get your claim backdated - ask your council .

items.name: Check & top up NI record
items.text: Anyone can check their NI record online for free via their Personal Tax Account. Gaps can be filled with voluntary Class 3 contributions. Critical to do before retirement.
items.action: Cite the page that says the online check is free and done through the Personal Tax Account, and drop 'anyone' and 'critical before retirement'.
items.reason: 'Anyone' and a single named route could mislead people who can't prove their identity online or who use a different sign-in or channel, though most people would still reach the check.

problems.claim: Anyone can check their NI record online for free via their Personal Tax Account.
problems.note: The text confirms you can check online, but it does not say the check is free, open to anyone, or done through a Personal Tax Account.
problems.quote: You can check your National Insurance record online to see:

problems.claim: It is critical to do this before retirement.
problems.note: The text never calls checking or topping up critical before retirement.

items.name: Free bus pass
items.text: Free off-peak bus travel anywhere in England from State Pension age. Also available to some disabled people. Apply via local council — usually processed in a few weeks.
items.action: Cite the English concessionary travel page for off-peak and England-wide travel, and remove the unsourced processing time.
items.reason: Off-peak, England-wide travel is probably correct, but the 'few weeks' processing time is invented and could mislead applicants about when their pass will arrive, since this varies by council.

problems.claim: The free travel is off-peak and covers anywhere in England.
problems.note: The text never says the travel is limited to off-peak times or that it covers all of England.

problems.claim: Applications are usually processed in a few weeks.
problems.note: The text gives no processing time.

items.name: Council Tax Reduction
items.text: A means-tested discount on your Council Tax bill. Administered by local councils — schemes vary by area. Can reduce the bill significantly or to zero on very low income.
items.action: Replace the 'to zero on very low income' wording with 'by up to 100%, depending on your council's scheme'.
items.reason: Some claimants, especially working-age ones in capped-scheme areas, could be misled about the amount of reduction they will receive.

problems.claim: It can reduce the bill significantly or to zero on very low income.
problems.note: A reduction of up to 100% is stated, but the text does not tie reducing the bill to zero to very low income.
problems.quote: Your bill could be reduced by up to 100%.

items.name: Social Tariff Broadband
items.text: Discounted broadband for people on UC, Pension Credit and other means-tested benefits. Available from major providers (BT, Virgin Media, Sky, etc.). Ofcom lists current prices from £10 to £24 a month. Anyone on Universal Credit qualifies with any provider; all major providers also accept Pension Credit, ESA, JSA and Income Support. The benefit claimant must be the main account holder.
items.action: Replace 'means-tested benefits' with 'some other benefits' and say that some providers also accept non-means-tested benefits such as Personal Independence Payment and Attendance Allowance.
items.reason: People who get only PIP or Attendance Allowance could wrongly conclude that they don't qualify, and miss providers whose social tariffs would accept them.

problems.claim: Social tariffs are discounted broadband for people on Universal Credit, Pension Credit and other means-tested benefits.
problems.note: The text says 'some other benefits' but never calls them means-tested, and it says some providers include benefits like Personal Independence Payment and Attendance Allowance.
problems.quote: Social tariffs are cheaper broadband and phone packages for people claiming Universal Credit, Pension Credit and some other benefits.

items.name: Funeral Expenses Payment
items.text: Helps pay for funeral costs if you or your partner receive a qualifying benefit such as Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, or Housing Benefit. Paid back from the deceased's estate if there are sufficient funds. Must claim within 6 months of the funeral.
items.action: Cite the full qualifying benefits list for Income Support, and say the payment is deducted from any money the claimant gets from the estate.
items.reason: Income Support is only one example on the list. Saying the payment is 'paid back when funds are sufficient' could mislead claimants who inherit money from the estate about how much they end up keeping.

problems.claim: It helps pay for funeral costs if you or your partner receive a qualifying benefit such as Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Income Support, or Housing Benefit.
problems.note: Universal Credit, Pension Credit and Housing Benefit are listed, but Income Support is not on the text's list of qualifying benefits.
problems.quote: You (or your partner) must get one or more of the following: Universal Credit income-related Employment and Support Allowance Pension Credit Housing Benefit

problems.claim: The payment is paid back from the deceased's estate if there are sufficient funds.
problems.note: The text says the payment is deducted from any money you get from the estate, not that it is paid back from the estate when it has enough funds.
problems.quote: Your Funeral Expenses Payment will be deducted from any money you get from the deceased’s estate.

items.name: Tell Us Once
items.text: Available in most of England, Wales and Scotland after a death is registered. Notifies up to 23 government organisations in a single interaction. Saves significant time and effort.
items.action: Remove 'most' and the 23 figure, and drop the unsourced time-saving claim.
items.reason: Saying the service covers only 'most' of England, Wales and Scotland could make some eligible people think it isn't available to them. The figure of 23 and the time-saving claim are background only.

problems.claim: Tell Us Once is available in most of England, Wales and Scotland after a death is registered.
problems.note: The text covers England, Scotland and Wales and says the death must be registered (or reported to a coroner), but it never says the service covers only 'most' of these areas.
problems.quote: You can use Tell Us Once if the person who died was living in England, Scotland or Wales.

problems.claim: It notifies up to 23 government organisations in a single interaction.
problems.note: The text says 'most government organisations in one go' but gives no figure of 23.
problems.quote: Tell Us Once is a service that lets you report a death to most government organisations in one go.

problems.claim: It saves significant time and effort.
problems.note: The text never says the service saves time or effort.

items.name: Legalise a document (apostille)
items.text: Available to anyone who needs a UK public document (birth certificate, marriage certificate, DBS check, etc.) officially recognised abroad. The document must be an original UK public document or certified copy.
items.action: Reword to include documents certified by a UK public official, such as notarised or solicitor-certified private documents.
items.reason: People with private documents such as contracts that a solicitor or notary has certified could wrongly be told they don't qualify.

problems.claim: The document must be an original UK public document or a certified copy.
problems.note: The source allows documents issued by UK public bodies or certified by a UK public official, which also covers non-public documents such as contracts, not only originals or certified copies of public documents.
problems.quote: You can also get other documents legalised, as long as they have been certified by a UK 'public official', such as a UK notary or solicitor.

items.name: Obtain death certificates
items.text: Anyone can order certified copies of a registered death. Death must have been registered first. Banks, probate and insurers all need originals.
items.action: Cite the official page on who can order certificates and that the death must be registered first, and say which nation the rule covers.
items.reason: Saying anyone can order is probably right for England and Wales, but it is unsourced and could mislead people whose death was registered in Scotland or Northern Ireland, where the process is different.

problems.claim: Anyone can order certified copies of a registered death.
problems.note: The text does not say who is eligible to order copies.

problems.claim: The death must have been registered before copies can be ordered.
problems.note: The text talks about copies of registered deaths but never says registration is required first.
problems.quote: You can also order certificates from the local register office where the birth, death or marriage was registered.

problems.claim: Banks, probate and insurers all need originals.
problems.note: The text does not mention banks, probate, insurers or originals.

items.name: National Insurance number
items.text: Needed for work and benefits in the UK, but you can start work before you receive it if you can prove your right to work, and you do not need one to start a benefit application. Apply online via DWP. Must have the right to work in the UK. UK citizens should already have one — applies mainly to new arrivals.
items.action: Replace the UK citizen and new arrivals claims with the Child Benefit condition for automatic issue.
items.reason: UK residents who were never sent a number because no Child Benefit claim was made could wrongly assume they already have one and not apply.

problems.claim: A National Insurance number is needed for work and benefits in the UK.
problems.note: The text says you need one to work, but for benefits it only says you may need one to get a benefit paid.
problems.quote: If you do not have a National Insurance number, you must apply for one if you plan to work.

problems.claim: You apply online via DWP.
problems.note: The text says you apply online but never names DWP.
problems.quote: To get a National Insurance number you need to apply online.

problems.claim: UK citizens should already have one.
problems.note: The text talks about UK residents who were sent a number because of a Child Benefit claim, not UK citizens in general, and it is conditional.
problems.quote: You’ll normally be sent a National Insurance number in the 3 months before your 16th birthday if both the following are true: you live in the UK a parent or guardian has filled in a Child Benefit claim form for you

problems.claim: The service applies mainly to new arrivals.
problems.note: The text never says the service is mainly for new arrivals.

items.name: Apply for a Gender Recognition Certificate
items.text: Available to adults (18+) who have, or have had, gender dysphoria; have lived in their acquired gender for at least 2 years; and intend to continue living in that gender until death. Medical evidence from two healthcare professionals is required.
items.action: Add that the gender dysphoria diagnosis must be made in the UK, and say that the two medical reports are needed on the standard route only, not the overseas route.
items.reason: Most applicants are diagnosed in the UK and use the standard route, so this is right for them, but people diagnosed abroad could be wrongly told they qualify, and overseas-route applicants would be told they need reports they don't.

problems.claim: Applicants must have, or have had, gender dysphoria.
problems.note: The source requires a gender dysphoria diagnosis made in the UK, and the claim leaves out that UK condition.
problems.quote: you’ve been diagnosed with gender dysphoria in the UK

problems.claim: Medical evidence from two healthcare professionals is required.
problems.note: The source asks for 2 reports from UK-registered doctors or a doctor and a clinical psychologist, but only on the main route; the overseas route does not need them.
problems.quote: You need 2 reports written by either: 2 different medical doctors registered in the UK a medical doctor and a clinical psychologist, both registered in the UK

items.name: Urgent passport application
items.text: Available to British nationals who need a passport urgently. Requires booking a passport office appointment. Premium (same-day) and Fast Track (1-week) options are available for an additional fee.
items.action: Cite an official passport eligibility page for the British nationality requirement and check whether it applies to this urgent service.
items.reason: Most people this affects are British citizens, for whom the claim is almost certainly right, but some groups, such as other types of British national or applicants outside the UK, may be told wrongly that they can use the urgent service.

problems.claim: It is available to British nationals.
problems.note: The urgent passport page never mentions British nationality; the linked pages that do are about other services.

items.name: Citizenship ceremony
items.text: All adults (18+) approved for British citizenship must attend a citizenship ceremony, organised by their local authority, within 3 months of receiving the Home Office invitation. Citizenship is not conferred until the ceremony is completed. The £130 ceremony fee is included in the £1,839 application fee.
items.action: Replace 'all adults' with the Windrush scheme exception, which lets those applicants choose not to attend.
items.reason: Windrush scheme citizens would be told wrongly that they must attend a ceremony. Other adult applicants are correctly told they must attend.

problems.claim: All adults (18+) approved for British citizenship must attend a citizenship ceremony.
problems.note: The text does make attendance a rule for successful applicants aged 18 or over, but it leaves out that Windrush scheme citizens can choose not to attend, so 'all' goes too far.
problems.quote: If you become a British citizen under the Windrush scheme you can choose if you want to attend a citizenship ceremony.

items.name: Get access to your eVisa
items.text: Required for most non-British, non-Irish nationals who have permission to stay in the UK. The eVisa is linked to your passport and UKVI account and proves your right to work, rent and access services.
items.action: Replace 'required for most' with the page's own list of who can use the service and who doesn't need an eVisa, and cite the guidance on linking your passport and on proving right to work and rent.
items.reason: Saying the eVisa is 'required for most non-British, non-Irish nationals' could wrongly tell some groups, such as people who don't need an eVisa, that they have to get one. The passport and right-to-work/rent points are probably accurate but need a source.

problems.claim: An eVisa is required for most non-British, non-Irish nationals who have permission to stay in the UK.
problems.note: The text lists who can use the service and who does not need an eVisa, but it never says the eVisa is required for most non-British, non-Irish nationals.

problems.claim: The eVisa is linked to your passport and your UKVI account.
problems.note: The text says the eVisa is linked to the UKVI account, but it only mentions a passport as something you may need to create the account, not as something the eVisa is linked to.
problems.quote: You cannot access your eVisa until you’ve linked it to your UKVI account.

problems.claim: The eVisa proves your right to work, rent and access services.
problems.note: The text says the eVisa proves immigration status, but it does not mention the right to work, rent or access services.
problems.quote: View your eVisa and get a share code to prove your immigration status

items.name: Report an error with your eVisa
items.text: Available to any eVisa holder who has found an error in their digital immigration status. Errors should be reported promptly as they can affect right-to-work and right-to-rent checks.
items.action: Replace 'any eVisa holder' with the situations the page says are covered and not covered, and cite a source for the right-to-work and right-to-rent point or remove it.
items.reason: Saying every eVisa holder with any error can use the service ignores the page's exclusions, so people in excluded situations could be told wrongly that they qualify. The advice to report promptly is only background.

problems.claim: The service is available to any eVisa holder who has found an error in their digital immigration status.
problems.note: The text lists specific situations the service covers and some it does not, so 'any' eVisa holder with any error overstates it.
problems.quote: When you should not use this service There’s a different way to:

problems.claim: Errors should be reported promptly.
problems.note: The text does not say anything about reporting quickly.

problems.claim: eVisa errors can affect right-to-work and right-to-rent checks.
problems.note: The text does not mention right-to-work or right-to-rent checks.

items.name: Indefinite Leave to Remain
items.text: Gives the right to live, work and study in the UK without immigration restrictions. Usually requires 5 years of lawful residence on an eligible visa. Must not have spent more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12-month period.
items.action: Say the 180-day absence limit applies to specific routes such as Skilled Worker and Scale-up, and cite the continuous residence guidance for each route.
items.reason: Most Skilled Worker applicants will get the right absence rule, but people on family or other routes may wrongly be told they don't qualify, or get the wrong absence rule, because the 180-day limit is presented as covering every route. The 'without immigration restrictions' wording is mostly phrasing, though the summary also leaves out that ILR can be lost after more than 2 years outside the UK.

problems.claim: Indefinite leave to remain gives the right to live, work and study in the UK without immigration restrictions.
problems.note: The text says ILR lets you live, work and study here for as long as you like, but it uses 'without immigration restrictions' only for right of abode, and it says ILR can be lost after more than 2 years outside the UK.
problems.quote: It gives you the right to live, work and study here for as long as you like, and apply for benefits if you’re eligible.

problems.claim: You must not have spent more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12-month period.
problems.note: The text states this rule for the Skilled Worker/T2 and Scale-up Worker routes, not as a rule for every ILR route.
problems.quote: You must have spent no more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12 months.

items.name: Life in the UK test
items.text: A 45-minute, 24-question test on British history, culture and values. Required before applying for Indefinite Leave to Remain or any route to British citizenship. Costs £50 per attempt. Exempt if under 18, over 65, or with certain long-term physical or mental conditions.
items.action: Change 'over 65' to '65 or over', drop 'any route' and cite a source for the history and values topics.
items.reason: 65-year-olds would wrongly be told they need the test and some citizenship applicants would be told it applies to them; the topic wording affects no one's outcome.

problems.claim: The test covers British history, culture and values.
problems.note: The source says the questions are about British traditions and customs; it does not mention history or values.
problems.quote: You’ll have 45 minutes to answer 24 questions about British traditions and customs.

problems.claim: The test is required for any route to British citizenship.
problems.note: The source says the test is needed for citizenship in general, but it does not say it applies to every route.
problems.quote: You need to take the test as part of your application for British citizenship or settlement in the UK.

problems.claim: You are exempt if you are over 65.
problems.note: The source's exemption is for people aged 65 or over, so people who are exactly 65 are also exempt, which 'over 65' leaves out.
problems.quote: are 65 or over

items.name: Skilled Worker dependant visa
items.text: Partners and children under 18 of a Skilled Worker visa holder can apply to join them in the UK as dependants, and can work and study without restriction. A visa fee is payable per dependant, plus the immigration health surcharge — check the current amounts on GOV.UK, as they change.
items.action: Cite the official page for dependants' work and study rights, remove "without restriction", and keep the check-current-fees advice as guidance.
items.reason: The overstated "without restriction" work claim could mislead some dependants about which jobs they can do; the advice to check current fees does not change what anyone pays.

problems.claim: Dependants can work and study without restriction.
problems.note: The source does not cover dependants' rights to work or study.

problems.claim: The amounts change, so check the current ones on GOV.UK.
problems.note: The source gives fee figures but does not say they change or tell readers to check the current amounts.

items.name: View or prove your immigration status
items.text: Available to non-British, non-Irish nationals with a UKVI account and eVisa. A share code is valid for 90 days and lets employers and landlords check your status; they will see some of your personal details.
items.action: Cite an official page saying British and Irish citizens do not use this service, or remove the nationality restriction.
items.reason: The nationality limit decides who is told they can use the service, so if it were wrong some people, such as Irish citizens or dual nationals, could be wrongly turned away.

problems.claim: The service is available to non-British, non-Irish nationals.
problems.note: The text does not say anything about which nationalities are eligible.

items.name: Voter Authority Certificate
items.text: Free photo ID for use at polling stations at UK elections, introduced from 2023. Required if you do not have an accepted form of photo ID (such as a passport, driving licence, or certain concessionary bus passes). Apply via your local council.
items.action: Limit the scope to England, Scotland and Wales, point Northern Ireland voters to the Electoral Identity Card, and cite a source for the 2023 date or remove it.
items.reason: Voters in Northern Ireland would be wrongly told this certificate covers their elections, when they need a different card.

problems.claim: It is free photo ID for use at polling stations at UK elections.
problems.note: The text limits it to England, Scotland and Wales, not the whole UK.
