items.name: Carer's leave (employer)
items.text: 5 days unpaid per year. Statutory right since April 2024.
items.action: Replace the fixed 5 days with one working week every 12 months, and cite the April 2024 start date.
items.reason: Part-time and irregular-hours employees would be told they get 5 days when they get one working week, e.g. 3 days if they work 3 days a week.

problems.claim: Carer's leave is 5 days unpaid per year.
problems.note: The text confirms unpaid leave every 12 months, but it sets the amount at one working week (for example 3 days for someone who works 3 days), not a fixed 5 days.
problems.quote: Employees can take up to one week of leave every 12 months. A ‘week’ means the length of time they usually work over 7 days.

problems.claim: It has been a statutory right since April 2024.
problems.note: The text gives no start date for the right.

items.name: Motability scheme
items.text: Car or scooter lease using mobility component. Requires Enhanced Rate PIP mobility.
items.action: Cite the Motability eligibility page and list all qualifying allowances, not only Enhanced Rate PIP mobility.
items.reason: Saying only Enhanced Rate PIP mobility qualifies could lead the agent to turn away people on DLA higher rate mobility, AFIP, WPMS or the Scottish Adult Disability Payment, even though these are probably true qualifying allowances.

problems.claim: The scheme provides a car or scooter lease using the mobility component.
problems.note: The text mentions leasing a vehicle with a qualifying mobility allowance, but it does not mention scooters or a 'mobility component' specifically.
problems.quote: Use your qualifying mobility allowance to lease a brand-new vehicle.

problems.claim: The scheme requires Enhanced Rate PIP mobility.
problems.note: The text only says 'qualifying mobility allowance' and does not name PIP or the Enhanced Rate.

items.name: Child Winter Heating Payment
items.text: £265.50 a year, paid from October, to help disabled children and young people in Scotland and their families with winter heating costs. Automatic — no application needed. Formerly Child Winter Heating Assistance.
items.action: Change "no application needed" to say most people do not need to apply, and cite the residency page for the Scotland requirement.
items.reason: The Scotland requirement is probably right, but saying no one needs to apply could stop the minority who do have to apply from ever getting the payment.

problems.claim: It helps disabled children and young people in Scotland and their families with winter heating costs.
problems.note: The purpose is stated, but the text never says the children must be in Scotland; it only says this is a Scottish Government benefit.
problems.quote: It’s a payment to help disabled children and young people and their families with increased heating costs over winter.

problems.claim: It is paid automatically and no application is needed.
problems.note: The text says most people do not need to apply, not that no one needs to.
problems.quote: Most people do not need to apply. You’ll get this payment automatically if you qualify.

items.name: Lasting Power of Attorney
items.text: Health and welfare and/or property and finance. Register before mental capacity is lost.
items.action: Change the text to say the donor must have capacity to make the LPA, and that an attorney can register it later.
items.reason: Families whose relative made an LPA but lost capacity before it was registered could wrongly think it is too late, when the attorney can still register it.

problems.claim: The LPA must be registered before mental capacity is lost.
problems.note: The text requires capacity when you make the LPA and when you register it yourself, but it also lets the attorney register it, so it never says registration must happen before capacity is lost.
problems.quote: You can apply to register your LPA yourself if you’re able to make your own decisions. Your attorney can also register it for you.

items.name: SR1 form (Special Rules for terminal illness)
items.text: A clinician completes the SR1 form for patients with a terminal illness (life expectancy under 12 months). It triggers fast-track processing for PIP, Attendance Allowance, ESA and UC — removing waiting periods and automatically awarding enhanced rates.
items.action: Cite the benefit pages for the four benefits and the waived waiting periods, and change 'automatically awarding enhanced rates' to 'higher payments in most cases'.
items.reason: Patients and families may expect the highest rate of every part of every benefit to be paid automatically, when the page only promises higher payments in most cases.

problems.claim: This applies to PIP, Attendance Allowance, ESA and UC.
problems.note: The text only says 'certain benefits' and never lists these four.

problems.claim: It removes waiting periods.
problems.note: The text does not mention waiting periods.

problems.claim: It automatically awards enhanced rates.
problems.note: The text says higher payments 'in most cases' but does not say they are awarded automatically or call them enhanced rates.
problems.quote: In most cases, the Special Rules allow people nearing the end of life to: get faster, easier access to certain benefits get higher payments for certain benefits

items.name: Housing Benefit
items.text: For pension-age renters not on Universal Credit. Claimed via local council. Means-tested, backdatable up to 3 months.
items.action: Add the new-claim route for people in supported, sheltered or temporary housing, and cite a source for the 3-month backdating limit or remove it.
items.reason: Working-age people in supported, sheltered or temporary housing would wrongly think they can't claim, and the backdating limit is stated without a source.

problems.claim: Housing Benefit is for pension-age renters not on Universal Credit.
problems.note: The text supports pension age and not already claiming Universal Credit, but it also allows new claims from people in supported, sheltered or temporary housing, and the claim leaves that out.
problems.quote: You can only make a new claim for Housing Benefit if either of the following apply: you have reached State Pension age you’re in supported, sheltered or temporary housing

problems.claim: It can be backdated by up to 3 months.
problems.note: The text says backdating may be possible but gives no 3-month limit.
problems.quote: You might also be able to get your claim backdated - ask your council .

items.name: Pension Credit
items.text: Tops up income to £238 a week (single). Gateway benefit — unlocks Winter Fuel Payment and free TV Licence.
items.action: Add the 75 or over condition to the free TV licence and cite a source for the Winter Fuel Payment link.
items.reason: Claimants under 75 could be told they will get a free TV licence when they will not, and the Winter Fuel Payment link has no source here.

problems.claim: Pension Credit unlocks Winter Fuel Payment.
problems.note: The source mentions Winter Fuel Payment only as something that does not count as income, not as help that Pension Credit unlocks.

problems.claim: Pension Credit unlocks a free TV Licence.
problems.note: The source limits the free TV licence to people aged 75 or over, and the claim leaves that condition out.
problems.quote: a free TV licence if you’re aged 75 or over

items.name: State Pension claim
items.text: Not automatic — must be actively claimed. Apply up to 4 months before State Pension age.
items.action: Cite the page giving the general 4-month claim window, or say that online claims need an invitation code requested within 3 months.
items.reason: People claiming online may try to start 4 months ahead and not be able to get an invitation code yet, though phone claimants are correctly advised.

problems.claim: You can apply up to 4 months before State Pension age.
problems.note: The 4-month window is given only for claiming by phone. For online claims the text only mentions requesting an invitation code within 3 months of State Pension age.
problems.quote: If you'll reach State Pension age in the next 4 months, you can phone the Pension Service to claim.

items.name: Free bus pass
items.text: Available from State Pension age. Apply via local council.
items.action: State that the qualifying age is 60 in Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and for London travel, and State Pension age elsewhere in England.
items.reason: People in Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland or London would be told they must wait until State Pension age when they can qualify at 60.

problems.claim: The free bus pass is available from State Pension age.
problems.note: State Pension age applies only in England; the text gives 60 for London travel, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
problems.quote: In England you can get a bus pass for free travel when you reach the State Pension age .

items.name: Council Tax Reduction
items.text: Apply to local council. Can reduce bill to zero on very low income.
items.action: Reword to say the bill can be reduced by up to 100% depending on the local council's scheme, without tying zero to very low income.
items.reason: Working-age people in areas whose schemes cap the reduction below 100% may expect a zero bill they will not get, though whether they qualify is unchanged.

problems.claim: It can reduce the bill to zero on very low income.
problems.note: The text says the bill can be cut by up to 100%, but it does not link a 100% reduction to having a very low income.
problems.quote: Your bill could be reduced by up to 100%.

items.name: Warm Home Discount
items.text: £150 off the electricity bill each winter. In England and Wales it is automatic for households getting Universal Credit, Housing Benefit, income-related ESA or Pension Credit. In Scotland some groups must apply to their supplier.
items.action: Say the discount is 'usually' automatic, and cite the England and Wales eligibility page for the nation split.
items.reason: Some people on these benefits don't get the discount automatically, so saying it is always automatic could leave them waiting instead of contacting the scheme or their supplier.

problems.claim: In England and Wales the discount is automatic for households getting Universal Credit, Housing Benefit, income-related ESA or Pension Credit.
problems.note: The page lists these four qualifying benefits and says you'll 'usually' get the discount automatically, but it never labels this list as the England and Wales criteria and does not say the discount is always automatic for all four.
problems.quote: The qualifying means-tested benefits are: Universal Credit Housing Benefit income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) Pension Credit

items.name: Bereavement Support Payment
items.text: If partner died, you are under State Pension age, and they had a NI record. Lump sum plus monthly payments.
items.action: Replace 'had a NI record' with the contribution condition (a certain amount of Class 1 or 2 contributions in one tax year) and add the work accident or work-related disease route.
items.reason: Most bereaved partners of people who worked would still get the right answer, but people whose partner had only NI credits or few contributions could be wrongly told they qualify, and people whose partner died from a work accident or disease could be wrongly told they don't.

problems.claim: The partner must have had a National Insurance record.
problems.note: The source asks for a certain amount of Class 1 or 2 contributions in one tax year, not just an NI record, and it also accepts death from a work accident or work-related disease instead.
problems.quote: paid a certain amount of Class 1 or Class 2 National Insurance contributions in any one tax year since 6 April 1975

items.name: Council Tax single person discount
items.text: 25% discount if now living alone after bereavement or separation.
items.action: Remove the bereavement or separation condition so the description covers anyone living alone as the only adult.
items.reason: Tying the discount to bereavement or separation could make people who live alone for other reasons think they don't qualify, though the core 25% for living alone is right.

problems.claim: The discount applies when you are living alone after a bereavement or separation.
problems.note: The text never mentions bereavement or separation as reasons for living alone.

items.name: Citizenship ceremony
items.text: Required final step after citizenship is approved. Make an oath of allegiance, receive your certificate. Must attend within 3 months of the Home Office invitation. Fee included in the citizenship application.
items.action: Say that attendance is required only for applicants aged 18 or over, and that Windrush applicants can choose whether to attend.
items.reason: Under-18s and Windrush scheme applicants could be told wrongly that they must attend. The 'final step' wording is only framing.

problems.claim: The citizenship ceremony is a required final step after citizenship is approved.
problems.note: The text says you must attend after a successful application, but only if you are 18 or over, and Windrush applicants can choose whether to attend; it never calls the ceremony the 'final step'.
problems.quote: You need to attend a citizenship ceremony if you’re 18 or over and have successfully applied to become a British citizen.

items.name: Report an error with your eVisa
items.text: Report incorrect information on your eVisa — such as a wrong name, conditions of stay or expiry date — to UKVI for correction.
items.action: Replace the examples with the ones the page gives: name, date of birth, nationality and immigration status.
items.reason: People whose conditions of stay or expiry date look wrong could be sent to this service when the page doesn't say it covers those errors, so some may use the wrong route.

problems.claim: Wrong conditions of stay or a wrong expiry date are examples of errors you can report.
problems.note: The text's examples are date of birth, immigration status, name and nationality. It does not mention conditions of stay or expiry dates.

items.name: Life in the UK test
items.text: Required for ILR and all citizenship routes (naturalisation, spouse, Irish citizen). 45-minute test, £50 per attempt. Exempt if under 18 or over 65.
items.action: Change 'over 65' to '65 or over' and replace 'all citizenship routes' with the routes the sources name.
items.reason: People who are exactly 65 would be told they must take the test when they are exempt, and people using citizenship routes that don't need the test (such as some registration routes) could be told they need it.

problems.claim: The test is required for all citizenship routes (naturalisation, spouse, Irish citizen).
problems.note: The source says the test is needed for citizenship in general, but it does not say this covers all routes or name naturalisation, spouse or Irish citizen routes.
problems.quote: You need to take the test as part of your application for British citizenship or settlement in the UK.

problems.claim: You are exempt if you are over 65.
problems.note: The source's exemption is for people aged 65 or over, so people who are exactly 65 are also exempt, which 'over 65' leaves out.
problems.quote: are 65 or over

items.name: Skilled Worker dependant visa
items.text: Family members (partner and children under 18) of a Skilled Worker visa holder can apply to join them in the UK as dependants. They can work and study without restriction.
items.action: Cite the dependants' page for work and study rights and remove "without restriction".
items.reason: Dependants can generally work and study, but "without restriction" overstates it: some roles, such as professional sportsperson or coach, are barred, so some dependants could be misled about which jobs they can take.

problems.claim: Dependants can work and study without restriction.
problems.note: The source does not say what dependants are allowed to do; it only lists what the main visa holder can do.

items.name: Student loan repayment
items.text: Student loan repayments are collected automatically via PAYE or Self Assessment once earnings exceed the plan threshold. Employees must declare their loan plan type to their employer on starting work.
items.action: Cite the GOV.UK page that says to tell your employer your plan type when you start work, or soften the wording to 'check your employer has you on the right plan'.
items.reason: Employees might think they have a legal duty to declare their plan type when they start a job. This would not change their repayments, but it could confuse what they have to do.

problems.claim: Employees must declare their loan plan type to their employer on starting work.
problems.note: The source only says you should check your employer has you on the right plan; it does not say you must declare the plan type when you start work.
problems.quote: You should check your employer has you on the correct repayment plan .

items.name: File annual accounts at Companies House
items.text: File your company's statutory annual accounts at Companies House; required for all limited companies each year.
items.action: Say the yearly requirement shown applies to private limited companies, or add what public companies must do.
items.reason: Most users run private limited companies and are described correctly, but public companies and other types could be misled by 'all limited companies'.

problems.claim: All limited companies must file annual accounts every year.
problems.note: The text sets this yearly requirement for private limited companies only and does not say it applies to all limited companies.
problems.quote: File annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after your company’s financial year ends

items.name: Waste carrier, broker or dealer registration
items.text: Any business that transports, buys, sells, or arranges disposal of waste in England must register with the Environment Agency. Lower-tier (free) covers own waste only; upper-tier covers commercial waste handling.
items.action: Redefine the tiers: upper tier also covers carrying your own construction or demolition waste, and lower tier covers more than just your own waste.
items.reason: Builders and other trades carrying their own construction or demolition waste could wrongly decide the free lower tier covers them, although this is only a summary line.

problems.claim: Lower-tier registration is free and covers your own waste only.
problems.note: The text says registration is usually free for transporting your own waste, but it never links this to 'lower tier' or defines what lower tier covers.
problems.quote: Registration is usually free if you only transport waste you produce yourself.

problems.claim: Upper-tier registration covers commercial waste handling.
problems.note: The text names an upper tier but never says what it covers, so 'commercial waste handling' is not stated.
problems.quote: When you register, you’ll be told whether your registration is ‘upper tier’ or ‘lower tier’.

items.name: Appeal to Tax Tribunal
items.text: Appeal an HMRC tax decision to the independent First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) if HMRC's review has not resolved the dispute.
items.action: Reword so an HMRC review is optional, not a condition for appealing to the tribunal.
items.reason: People who can go straight to the tribunal, such as those with indirect tax decisions or those who turn down a review, could be told to wait for a review they don't need and lose time.

problems.claim: The appeal is for when HMRC's review has not resolved the dispute.
problems.note: The text says you can appeal after a review you disagree with, but it treats a review as optional, not a condition for appealing.
problems.quote: If you do not agree with the outcome you can still appeal to the tribunal.

items.name: Register for Corporation Tax
items.text: Required within 3 months of starting to trade. Applies to limited companies, and to unincorporated organisations such as clubs and associations that become active.
items.action: Say the 3 months run from the start of the first accounting period (usually when the company starts to do business), or cite the page that says 'starting to do business'.
items.reason: For most companies, starting to trade and the start of the first accounting period are the same date, but where they differ the deadline could be worked out from the wrong date.

problems.claim: Registration is required within 3 months of starting to trade.
problems.note: The text sets the 3-month period from the start of the tax accounting period, for a company that is active and within the charge to Corporation Tax. It does not say 'starting to trade'.
problems.quote: You must tell HMRC within 3 months of starting your tax accounting period if your limited company is within the charge of Corporation Tax and is now active.

items.name: Making Tax Digital enrolment
items.text: Mandatory for VAT-registered businesses, which should now all be signed up automatically. Phased rollout for income tax from 2026.
items.action: Cite the official Making Tax Digital for Income Tax page for the 2026 rollout.
items.reason: Self-employed people and landlords could be misled about whether MTD applies to their income tax if the unsourced 2026 rollout claim were wrong, though VAT businesses are not affected.

problems.claim: There is a phased rollout for income tax from 2026.
problems.note: The sources only cover MTD for VAT and never mention income tax or 2026.

items.name: Scrap metal dealer licence
items.text: Any person or business buying, selling, or storing scrap metal in England and Wales must hold a licence from their local council. Cash payments are prohibited; all transactions must be by bank transfer.
items.action: Change the payment sentence so it says only that dealers must not pay cash for scrap metal, without claiming every transaction must be by bank transfer.
items.reason: Dealers could wrongly think they must refuse cash when selling scrap, or that other non-cash ways of paying for scrap, such as cheques, are banned, though anyone who pays by bank transfer still complies.

problems.claim: All transactions must be by bank transfer.
problems.note: The source names a bank account for paying for scrap metal and bans cash purchases, but it never says every transaction must be a bank transfer.
problems.quote: details of the bank account that will be used to pay for scrap metal

items.name: Street trading licence
items.text: Anyone selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales generally requires a street trading licence from their local council. Councils may restrict hours, location or days.
items.action: Change 'generally requires' to 'may need' a licence and cite a source for location restrictions or remove them.
items.reason: Some traders may be told they need a licence when their council does not require one for their street. Most people are still sent to their council, which is the right place to check.

problems.claim: Anyone selling goods or services from a street or public place in England and Wales generally requires a street trading licence from their local council.
problems.note: The text only says you 'may need' a licence to trade in the street; it does not say one is generally required, and it does not mention goods or services or public places.
problems.quote: You may need to get a licence to trade in the street in England and Wales

problems.claim: Councils may restrict hours, location or days.
problems.note: The text says councils can restrict days and times but says nothing about restricting location.
problems.quote: give you one for fewer days and times than you asked for

items.name: Register as a childminder with Ofsted
items.text: Mandatory Ofsted registration for anyone who wants to childmind in England for payment. Takes up to 12 weeks. Requires DBS check, first aid training and a health declaration.
items.action: Say registration applies to care of under-8s for more than 2 hours a day, and add the childminder agency route.
items.reason: Most childminders do need to register, but people who only care for older children or for short periods are wrongly told it is mandatory, and people who would prefer an agency are not told that route exists.

problems.claim: Ofsted registration is mandatory for anyone who wants to childmind in England for payment.
problems.note: Registration is only required when the children are under 8 and cared for more than 2 hours a day, and you can register with a childminder agency instead of Ofsted, so it is not mandatory Ofsted registration for anyone paid to childmind.
problems.quote: You must register as a childminder if all of the following apply: the children are under the age of 8 you look after them for more than 2 hours a day you get paid to look after them

items.name: Employers' Liability Insurance
items.text: Legal requirement if employing anyone. Minimum £5m cover.
items.action: Replace 'anyone' with a statement that there are exemptions, such as employing only a family member or staff based outside England, Scotland and Wales.
items.reason: Employers whose only employee is a family member, or whose staff are based outside Great Britain, would wrongly be told they must buy cover.

problems.claim: Employers' liability insurance is a legal requirement if you employ anyone.
problems.note: The text says employers must get it, but it lists exemptions (only employing a family member, or someone based outside England, Scotland and Wales), so 'anyone' goes too far.
problems.quote: You must get Employers’ Liability ( EL ) insurance: as soon as you become an employer

items.name: Lifetime ISA withdrawal
items.text: Claim 25% government bonus. Conveyancer requests from ISA provider before completion.
items.action: Cite the official Lifetime ISA home-buying guidance showing the conveyancer asks the provider for the funds before completion.
items.reason: First-time buyers use this to decide who asks for the money and when. If it were wrong, they could wait for their conveyancer and miss the funds at completion.

problems.claim: The conveyancer requests the funds from the ISA provider before completion.
problems.note: The text says the provider pays the funds straight to the conveyancer, but it does not say the conveyancer makes the request or that this happens before completion.
problems.quote: you use a conveyancer or solicitor to act for you in the purchase - the ISA provider will pay the funds directly to them

items.name: Stamp Duty Land Tax return
items.text: File within 14 days of completion. Solicitor usually handles. Required even if no tax is due.
items.action: Replace the blanket 'required even if no tax is due' with the actual rule and list the exemptions where no return is needed.
items.reason: Buyers of exempt transactions, such as freeholds under £40,000 or property left in a will, would be told to file a return they do not need, though most buyers under £40,000 or claiming relief do need one.

problems.claim: A return is required even if no tax is due.
problems.note: The text requires a return with no tax due only in some cases, such as claiming relief or most transactions under £150,000, and lists exemptions where no return is needed, so the blanket rule is not stated.
problems.quote: You must complete an SDLT return to claim relief, even if no tax is due.

items.name: Land Registry registration (AP1)
items.text: Register new ownership. Solicitor handles. Required for mortgage to complete.
items.action: Say that owners can apply themselves or use a solicitor, and remove the claim that registration is needed for a mortgage to complete.
items.reason: People doing their own conveyancing may think only a solicitor can apply, and buyers may wrongly believe registration must happen before their mortgage completes.

problems.claim: A solicitor handles the application.
problems.note: The text says a solicitor or conveyancer can do it, but so can you, so it is not always the solicitor.
problems.quote: You can apply to register a property yourself or get a solicitor or conveyancer to do it for you.

problems.claim: Registration is required for a mortgage to complete.
problems.note: The text says mortgaged property must be registered, but never says registration is needed for a mortgage to complete.

items.name: New Style ESA
items.text: If health prevents work. Requires fit note from GP and Work Capability Assessment.
items.action: Say a fit note is needed only after more than 7 days off work, remove 'from GP', and say an assessment may be needed.
items.reason: People off work for 7 days or less, or whose fit note comes from another healthcare professional, or who don't need an assessment, could think they can't apply or must wait.

problems.claim: It requires a fit note from a GP.
problems.note: A fit note is needed only if you have been unable to work for more than 7 days in a row, and the text does not say it must come from a GP.
problems.quote: a fit note (sometimes called a ‘sick note’ or a ‘statement of fitness for work’) if you’ve not been able to work for more than 7 days in a row because of a disability or health condition

problems.claim: It requires a Work Capability Assessment.
problems.note: The text says an assessment may be needed and that some people do not need one, so it is not always required.
problems.quote: After you’ve made your claim, you’ll be told if you need to have a ‘Work Capability Assessment’ and what group you’ll be put in.

items.name: Best Start Grant
items.text: Three one-off payments for families on qualifying benefits in Scotland: Pregnancy and Baby Payment (£796.65 first child, £398.35 others), Early Learning Payment (£331.95), School Age Payment (£331.95).
items.action: Cite the official page that lists the qualifying benefits, such as Universal Credit, and name them.
items.reason: The benefits requirement decides who qualifies, but this summary field never names the benefits, so someone could not tell from it whether they are eligible.

problems.claim: The payments are for families on qualifying benefits.
problems.note: The text does not say which benefits, if any, you need to be getting.

items.name: Free School Meals
items.text: From the 2026-27 academic year, auto-eligible for any household on Universal Credit, regardless of income. Also available via income-related ESA, Pension Credit or immigration support benefits. Apply via school or local authority.
items.action: Change 'Pension Credit' to 'the guarantee element of Pension Credit' and say to apply through the local authority.
items.reason: Pensioner carers who get only Savings Credit would be told wrongly that they qualify, and some people may go to the school to apply when the council is the stated route.

problems.claim: Free school meals are also available via income-related ESA, Pension Credit or immigration support benefits.
problems.note: The text limits this to the guaranteed element of Pension Credit, but the claim says Pension Credit in general.
problems.quote: income-related Employment and Support Allowance support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 the guaranteed element of Pension Credit

problems.claim: You apply via the school or the local authority.
problems.note: The text names the local authority's website as the way to apply; it only mentions the school as a place to ask about eligibility, not as a way to apply.
problems.quote: find out how to apply on your local authority’s website

items.name: Raise concerns about a school with Ofsted
items.text: Report serious concerns about a school or college to Ofsted after exhausting the school's internal complaints procedure. Ofsted can bring forward an inspection if warranted.
items.action: Remove the colleges, 'serious' and inspection-brought-forward claims, and say Ofsted may look at the complaint at the next inspection.
items.reason: People with college concerns may be sent to the wrong route, the word 'serious' may put off some valid complainants, and complainants may expect an early inspection that the pages don't promise.

problems.claim: You can report serious concerns about a school or college to Ofsted.
problems.note: The text covers complaints about state schools, but it does not mention colleges and does not say concerns must be 'serious'.
problems.quote: Use this service to complain to Ofsted about a state school, including academies and free schools.

problems.claim: Ofsted can bring forward an inspection if warranted.
problems.note: The text only says Ofsted may discuss the complaint at the school's next inspection. It says nothing about bringing an inspection forward.

items.name: Make a SORN
items.text: Free Statutory Off Road Notification — required when a vehicle is taken off the road and not being taxed. Tax is cancelled and remaining full months refunded. SORN stays active until the vehicle is taxed again. Using a SORNed vehicle on a public road can lead to prosecution and a fine of up to £2,500.
items.action: State that a SORN also ends when the vehicle is sold, permanently exported or scrapped, and cite a source showing SORN is free.
items.reason: Keepers who sell, export or scrap a vehicle may wrongly think the SORN carries on. The 'free' claim is probably true but has no source here.

problems.claim: A Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN) is free.
problems.note: None of the sources gives a cost for making a SORN. The only fee mentioned is £25 for a new log book.

problems.claim: The SORN stays active until the vehicle is taxed again.
problems.note: The text says the SORN also ends if the vehicle is sold, permanently exported or scrapped, not only when it is taxed again.
problems.quote: Your SORN is automatically cancelled when you tax your vehicle again or if you sell, permanently export or scrap your vehicle .

items.name: Driving Test (practical)
items.text: Must pass theory test first. £62 (weekday) or £75 (evening/weekend). On passing, DVLA usually sends the full licence automatically. Must claim within 2 years of passing or the pass lapses and you must retake.
items.action: Say the examiner offers to have the licence sent automatically, and apply the 2-year limit only to people who do not take that option.
items.reason: Anyone who turns down automatic sending needs the 2-year limit, and calling it the usual outcome could leave some unsure whether they must apply; the retake rule after 2 years is probably on another official page.

problems.claim: When you pass, DVLA usually sends the full licence automatically.
